== Symbologies Reference

=== Point of Sale

==== EAN-13

*EAN-13* is an extension of the <<_upc_a,UPC-A>> barcode symbology that
usually carries a GTIN-13.

An EAN-13 whose first digit is 0 has the same bars as the
<<_upc_a,UPC-A>> carrying the remaining twelve digits: EAN-13 encodes
its leading digit by mirroring some of the symbol characters in the left
half, and for a leading 0 none are mirrored.

Also known as: EAN, European Article Number, International Article
Number, JAN, JAN-13, IAN, WPC, SAAN, UCCET, ABAC, BCCI, ICA, MANA, KANC,
ANA, ANC.

Misnomers: UCC-13, GTIN-13.

Uses:

* Retail products scanned at point of sale.
* In-store items, such as weighed goods with price-embedded labels from
a scale, using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 02, 04 or 20 to
29).
* Store, national and euro coupons (beginning 99, or 981 to 983).

Variants:

* EAN-13{plus}2 is an extension of EAN-13 that includes a
<<_ean_2,two-digit add-on>>.
* EAN-13{plus}5 is an extension of EAN-13 that includes a
<<_ean_5,five-digit add-on>>.
* EAN-99 is a special form of EAN-13 starting with `99` that is used as
an in-store coupon.
* <<_ean_8,EAN-8>> is a barcode symbology derived from EAN-13 that is
designed for small packaging. It uses a distinct numbering system based
on GTIN-8.
* <<_isbn,ISBN>> is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify books.
* <<_ismn,ISMN>> is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify printed music.
* <<_issn,ISSN>> is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify periodicals.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,EAN-13 Composite>> is a variant of EAN-13
that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 Composite 2D component is
required.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field for an EAN-13 may contain twelve or thirteen digits,
optionally followed by a space then two or five digits if an
<<_ean_2,EAN-2>> or <<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on is required.
* If twelve digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is
calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The *guarddescent* option controls how far the guard bars extend below
the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
* The *addondescent* option controls how far the add-on bars extend
below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the
value of *guarddescent*).

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    9520123456788
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13
....

....
Data:    952012345678
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13
....

==== EAN-8

*EAN-8* is derived from the <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> barcode symbology and is
designed for small packaging. It usually carries a GTIN-8.

A GTIN-8 is assigned individually, on request, by a GS1 Member
Organisation for an item whose packaging is too small for an EAN-13.

Also known as: JAN-8.

Misnomers: UCC-8.

Uses:

* Retail products whose packaging is too small for an EAN-13.
* In-store items using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 0 or
2).

Variants:

* EAN-Velocity is a special form of EAN-8 starting with `0` that is used
for numbering items within a company.
* <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> is a longer variant of EAN-8 which has a distinct
number system based on GTIN-13.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,EAN-8 Composite>> is a variant of EAN-8 that
should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is
required.
* EAN-8{plus}2 is a *non-standard* extension of EAN-8 that includes a
<<_ean_2,two-digit add-on>>.
* EAN-8{plus}5 is a *non-standard* extension of EAN-8 that includes a
<<_ean_5,five-digit add-on>>.
* <<_marks__spencer,Marks & Spencer>> is a derivative of EAN-8 used by
the UK retailer.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field takes either seven or eight digits.
* When the *permitaddon* option is provided, the initial seven or eight
digits can be followed by a space then two or five digits where a
<<_ean_2,EAN-2>> or <<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on is required
(*non-standard*).
* If seven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is
calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The *guarddescent* option controls how far the guard bars extend below
the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
* The *addondescent* option controls how far the add-on bars extend
below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the
value of *guarddescent*).

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    95200002
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean8
....

....
Data:    9520000
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean8
....

==== UPC-A

The *UPC-A* barcode symbology is used for identification of retail goods
at point of sale. It usually carries a GTIN-12.

A UPC-A has the same bars as an <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> whose first digit is
0. EAN-13 encodes its additional leading digit by mirroring some of the
symbol characters in the left half, and for a leading 0 none are
mirrored.

Also known as: UPC, Universal Product Code.

Misnomers: UCC-12.

Uses:

* Retail products scanned at point of sale, chiefly in the US and
Canada.
* In-store items, such as weighed goods with price-embedded labels from
a scale, using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 2 or 4).

Variants:

* UPC-A{plus}2 is an extension of UPC-A that includes a
<<_ean_2,two-digit add-on>>.
* UPC-A{plus}5 is an extension of UPC-A that includes a
<<_ean_5,five-digit add-on>>.
* <<_upc_e,UPC-E>> is a barcode symbology derived from UPC-A that is
designed for small packaging.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,UPC-A Composite>> is a variant of UPC-A that
should be used when a CC-A or CC-B
<<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 composite>> 2D component is required.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field for a UPC-A may contain eleven or twelve digits,
optionally followed by a space then two or five digits if an
<<_ean_2,EAN-2>> or <<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on is required.
* Alternatively, the data field may contain seven or eight digits of a
<<_upc_e,UPC-E>> to produce the equivalent UPC-A symbol.
* If eleven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is
calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The *guarddescent* option controls how far the guard bars extend below
the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
* The *addondescent* option controls how far the add-on bars extend
below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the
value of *guarddescent*).

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    012345000058
Options: includetext
Encoder: upca
....

....
Data:    01234500005
Options: includetext
Encoder: upca
....

==== UPC-E

*UPC-E* is a compacted form of the <<_upc_a,UPC-A>> barcode symbology
that usually carries a GTIN-12 that has been zero compressed.

Also known as: UPC-E0.

Uses:

* Retail products whose packaging is too small for a UPC-A.

Variants:

* UPC-E{plus}2 is an extension of UPC-E that includes a
<<_ean_2,two-digit add-on>>.
* UPC-E{plus}5 is an extension of UPC-E that includes a
<<_ean_5,five-digit add-on>>.
* <<_upc_a,UPC-A>> is the full size form of UPC-E.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,UPC-E Composite>> is a variant of UPC-E that
should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 Composite 2D component is
required.
* UPC-E1 is a UPC-E with a number system of _1_. This is not defined by
any symbology standard.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field takes either seven or eight digits, optionally followed
by a space then two or five digits if an <<_ean_2,EAN-2>> or
<<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on is required.
* Alternatively, the data field may contain eleven or twelve digits of a
<<_upc_a,UPC-A>> to produce the equivalent UPC-E symbol, provided that
the input can be zero suppressed.
* If seven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is
calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* The primary data must start with "0", or "1" for a UPC-E1.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guarddescent* option controls how far the guard bars extend below
the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
* The *addondescent* option controls how far the add-on bars extend
below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the
value of *guarddescent*).

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    01234558
Options: includetext
Encoder: upce
....

....
Data:    0123455
Options: includetext
Encoder: upce
....

==== ISBN

An *ISBN* barcode is a variant of <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> that is used to
identify books.

Also known as: ISBN-13, International Standard Book Number, Bookland
EAN, Bookland EAN-13.

Uses:

* Books.

Variants:

* ISBN-10 is a legacy format that was deprecated for public use after
1st January 2007.

Standards: ISO 2108, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data should contain twelve or thirteen digits separated
appropriately by dash characters _-_.
* The data can also be provided in legacy ISBN-10 format as nine or ten
digits separated appropriately by dash characters _-_. This will be
automatically upgraded to the ISBN-13 format.
* If the last digit of the primary data is not given then the ISBN check
digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
* The primary data can optionally be followed by a space then five
digits if an <<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on is required, typically to encode
the book's price (see Price Add-On below).
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The following options control the placement and styling of the ISBN
text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding
`extratext++*++` option:
** *isbntext*: Override the ISBN label content
** *isbntextfont*: PostScript font name for text above symbol
** *isbntextsize*: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
** *isbntextcolor*: Colour for the text above symbol
** *isbntextxalign*, *isbntextyalign*: Alignment of the text above
symbol
** *isbntextxoffset*, *isbntextyoffset*: Position of the text above
symbol, in points
** *isbntextdirection*: Direction of the text above symbol
** *isbntextgaps*: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in
points
** *isbntextsubspace*, *isbntextsplit*, *isbntextlinegaps*: See
<<_text_properties,Text Properties>>
* _Deprecated._ The *legacy* option shows the ISBN-10 above the symbol
in place of the ISBN-13. The bars are the same.

===== Price Add-On

A five-digit add-on encodes the book's price as a currency digit
followed by four digits of price, under conventions set by each market's
book industry. The International ISBN Agency's users' manual says the
add-on carries a price only in the United States and Canada, and that
elsewhere it may be used for a publisher's in-house purposes. Check the
local convention with the ISBN agency or trading partners.

[cols=",",options="header",]
|===
|Add-on |Conventional Meaning
|`00001` to `09999` |Price in pounds sterling, £0.01 to £99.99

|`10000` to `49999` |Price in US dollars, US$100.00 to US$499.99

|`50001` to `59998` |Price in US dollars, US$0.01 to US$99.98

|`59999` |Formerly, a price in US dollars above US$99.98 (US$99.99
cannot be encoded)

|`60001` to `69999` |Price in Canadian dollars, CA$0.01 to CA$99.99

|`90000` to `98999` |For the publisher's own in-house use, such as
handling returns

|`99990` |A used book (US college stores)

|`99991` |A desk copy (US college stores)
|===

* In the UK, booksellers look up a book's price from its ISBN, so the
symbol without an add-on is generally recommended. UK publishers selling
into the US add the US price.
* In Korea, the add-on carries the Korean book number's additional code
rather than a price: a readership digit, a publication form digit and a
three-digit subject classification from the Korean Decimal
Classification.
* Sources:
https://www.isbn-international.org/sites/default/files/ISBN%20Manual%202012%20-corr.pdf[International
ISBN Agency&#44; ISBN Users' Manual];
https://www.bisg.org/barcoding-guidelines-for-the-us-book-industry[Book
Industry Study Group&#44; Barcoding Guidelines for the US Book
Industry];
https://bic.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/2019.05.31-Bar-Coding-for-Books-rev-09.pdf[Book
Industry Communication&#44; Bar Coding for Books];
https://booknetcanada.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UserDocs/pages/1378342/Product+Bar+Codes[BookNet
Canada&#44; Product Bar Codes];
https://www.isbn-international.org/sites/default/files/Korean_ISBN_and_ISSN_manual.pdf[National
Library of Korea&#44; Korean ISBN and ISSN Manual].

===== Examples

====== ISBN-13

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISBN check digit:

....
Data:    978-1-873671-00-9
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn
....

....
Data:    978-1-873671-00
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn
....

====== Styling the ISBN label

The ISBN label can be styled using the `isbntext++*++` options (or the
equivalent `extratext++*++`):

....
Data:    978-1-873671-00-9
Options: includetext isbntextcolor=FF0000 isbntextxalign=center
Encoder: isbn
....

==== ISMN

An *ISMN* barcode is a variant of <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> with a prefix _979_
that is used to identify printed music.

Also known as: International Standard Music Number, ISMN-13, Musicland
EAN-13.

Uses:

* Printed music.

Variants:

* ISMN-10 is a legacy format that was deprecated for public use.

Standards: ISO 10957, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data should contain twelve or thirteen digits separated
appropriately by dash characters _-_.
* The data can also be provided in legacy ISMN-10 format start _M-_ then
eight or nine digits separated appropriately by dash characters _-_.
This will be automatically upgraded to the ISMN-13 format.
* If the last digit of the primary data is not given then the ISMN check
digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
* The primary data can optionally be followed by a space and two or five
digits for an <<_ean_2,EAN-2>> or <<_ean_5,EAN-5>> add-on.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The following options control the placement and styling of the ISMN
text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding
`extratext++*++` option:
** *ismntext*: Override the ISMN label content
** *ismntextfont*: PostScript font name for text above symbol
** *ismntextsize*: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
** *ismntextcolor*: Colour for the text above symbol
** *ismntextxalign*, *ismntextyalign*: Alignment of the text above
symbol
** *ismntextxoffset*, *ismntextyoffset*: Position of the text above
symbol, in points
** *ismntextdirection*: Direction of the text above symbol
** *ismntextgaps*: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in
points
** *ismntextsubspace*, *ismntextsplit*, *ismntextlinegaps*: See
<<_text_properties,Text Properties>>
* _Deprecated._ The *legacy* option shows the ISMN-10 above the symbol
in place of the ISMN-13. The bars are the same.

===== Examples

====== ISMN-13

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISMN check digit:

....
Data:    979-0-2600-0043-8
Options: includetext
Encoder: ismn
....

....
Data:    979-0-2600-0043
Options: includetext

====== Styling the ISMN label

The ISMN label can be styled using the `ismntext++*++` options (or the
equivalent `extratext++*++`):

....
Data:    979-0-2600-0043-8
Options: includetext ismntextcolor=FF0000 ismntextxalign=center
Encoder: ismn
....

==== ISSN

An *ISSN* barcode is an <<_ean_13,EAN-13>> with prefix _977_ used to
identify periodicals.

Also known as: International Standard Serial Number.

Uses:

* Magazines, newspapers and other periodicals, with the issue number in
an add-on.

Standards: ISO 3297, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data should contain the seven or eight digits ISSN separated by a
dash character _-_, optionally followed by a two-digit sequence variant
(`00` when not given; it usually starts at zero and is incremented
whenever the recommended retail price is amended), and then optionally
by two or five digits if a <<_ean_2,two-digit add-on>> or
<<_ean_5,five-digit add-on>> is required.
** The add-on usually indicates the issue number, according to the
https://www.issn.org/understanding-the-issn/issn-uses/identification-with-the-ean-13-barcode/[ISSN
International Centre].
** In the UK, the
https://ppa.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/PPA_Best_Practice_for_Bar_Code_Guidelines.pdf[PPA's
barcoding guidelines] specify a two-digit add-on identifying each issue.
** A five-digit add-on can be used instead of a two-digit one where the
publisher's numbering needs it, such as the actual date of issue,
according to the https://ref.gs1.org/standards/genspecs/[GS1 General
Specifications]. The two cannot be used together.
* If the last digit of the ISSN data is not given then the ISSN check
digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.
* The *guardwhitespace* option enables the display of whitespace guard
marks.
* The following options control the placement and styling of the ISSN
text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding
`extratext++*++` option:
** *issntext*: Override the ISSN label content
** *issntextfont*: PostScript font name for text above symbol
** *issntextsize*: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
** *issntextcolor*: Colour for the text above symbol
** *issntextxalign*, *issntextyalign*: Alignment of the text above
symbol
** *issntextxoffset*, *issntextyoffset*: Position of the text above
symbol, in points
** *issntextdirection*: Direction of the text above symbol
** *issntextgaps*: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in
points
** *issntextsubspace*, *issntextsplit*, *issntextlinegaps*: See
<<_text_properties,Text Properties>>

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISSN check digit
and having sequence variant _00_:

....
Data:    0317-8471 00
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn
....

....
Data:    0317-847 00
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn

=== Two-Dimensional

==== Aztec Code

*Aztec Code* is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology. It can encode full
256-character extended-ASCII.

Uses:

* Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
* European rail tickets (UIC Flexible Content Barcode).

Variants:

* <<_compact_aztec_code,Compact Aztec Code>> is a reduced form of Aztec
Code used in applications where the space for the symbol is restricted.
* <<_aztec_runes,Aztec Runes>> are a set of small barcode symbols that
are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the percentage of error
correction to be applied when expanding the data, from `5` to `95`, by
default `23`.
* The *ecaddchars* option is used to specify how many additional error
correction characters to add after applying the eclevel percentage, `3`
or more, by default `3`.
* The *layers* option is used to specify a particular number of layers
in which to encode the data, between `1` and `32`. By default the
encoder will create a symbol with the minimal number of layers to encode
the given data.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. Reader programming is only compatible
with 1- to 22-layer full-range Aztec Code symbols, so *layers* must also
be given, from `1` to `22`.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
a pre-encoded bitstream suitable for direct low-level encoding.
* _Deprecated: Consider <<_compact_aztec_code,Compact Aztec Code>>
instead._ The *format* option can also be used to create Compact Aztec
Code symbols, using `format=compact`.
* _Deprecated: Consider <<_aztec_runes,Aztec Runes>> instead._ The
*format* option can also be used to create Aztec Code "runes", using
`format=rune`. In this case the rune symbol number should be given in
the data field.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 26 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. *sampos* and *samtotal* are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is an optional message ID, which is the same in every symbol
of the sequence and must not contain spaces. Uppercase letters encode
most compactly.
** Structured Append is not available for Aztec Runes, reader
initialisation symbols or with the *raw* option.

===== Examples

A symbol with a fixed number of layers:

....
Data:    ABC123
Options: layers=3
Encoder: azteccode
....

==== Compact Aztec Code

*Compact Aztec Code* is a reduced form of the <<_aztec_code,Aztec Code>>
barcode that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is
restricted.

Variants:

* <<_aztec_code,Aztec Code>> is the larger, more popular variant.
* <<_aztec_runes,Aztec Runes>> are a set of small barcode symbols that
are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the percentage of error
correction to be applied when expanding the data, from `5` to `95`, by
default `23`.
* The *ecaddchars* option is used to specify how many additional error
correction characters to add after applying the eclevel percentage, `3`
or more, by default `3`.
* The *layers* option is used to specify a particular number of layers
in which to encode the data, between `1` and `4`. By default the encoder
will create a symbol with the minimal number of layers to encode the
given data.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. Reader programming is only compatible
with 1-layer Compact Aztec Code symbols.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
a pre-encoded bitstream suitable for direct low-level encoding.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 26 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. *sampos* and *samtotal* are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is an optional message ID, which is the same in every symbol
of the sequence and must not contain spaces. Uppercase letters encode
most compactly.
** Structured Append is not available for reader initialisation symbols
or with the *raw* option.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    This is Compact Aztec Code
Options:
Encoder: azteccodecompact
....

==== Aztec Runes

*Aztec Runes* are a set of small <<_aztec_code,Aztec Code>> symbols that
are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains the rune number `0` to `255`.

===== Examples

A rune encoding the value _25_:

....
Data:    25
Options:
Encoder: aztecrune
....

==== Data Matrix

The *Data Matrix* symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode that can encode
full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Data Matrix ECC 200, DataMatrix.

Uses:

* Marking small parts and electronic components, and direct part
marking.
* Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
* Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU
traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
* US military part marking under the Department of Defense IUID rules
(MIL-STD-130), carrying an ISO/IEC 15434 message.
* German pharmacy packs under securPharm in the IFA format, carrying the
PPN in an ISO/IEC 15434 message.
* Electronic component reel and bag labels (ECIA EIGP 114).
* Postage printed by franking machines, online and on stamps, such as
Deutsche Post's Matrixcode.
* Blood, tissue and cell products labelled to ISBT 128.
* Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG
B-16, VDA 4994).
* Aircraft parts, marked to ATA Spec 2000 Chapter 9 (SAE AS9132).
* Back-surface marking of silicon wafers (SEMI T7).

Variants:

* <<_data_matrix_rectangular,Data Matrix Rectangular>> is a variant of
Data Matrix that uses rectangular symbols.
* <<_data_matrix_rectangular_extension,Data Matrix Rectangular Extension>>
is a variant of Data Matrix Rectangular that provides a greater range of
symbol dimensions.
* <<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>> is a variant of Data Matrix that
should be used when encoding data that is in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* <<_gs1_digital_link_data_matrix,GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix>> is a
variant of Data Matrix that should be used when encoding a GS1 Digital
Link URI.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC Data Matrix>> is a variant of Data Matrix that
should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
* <<_mailmark,Royal Mail Mailmark>> is a variant of Data Matrix that is
used by the Royal Mail postal service on letters and other small
mailpieces.
* <<_ppn_code,PPN-Code>> is a variant of Data Matrix that carries the
Pharmacy Product Number and pack data of pharmaceutical packs.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is
useful for specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider
<<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>> for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^PROG`: PROG - Reader programming
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06,
except in a Structured Append symbol.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same
in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one
message from those of another.
** An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the
whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
** FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
** Structured Append is not available with the *raw* option or reader
programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix, Royal
Mail Mailmark or PPN-Code symbols.
* When the *dotty* option is specified the modules are rendered as dots
rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the
*inkspread* option.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol.
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC`. Valid options are _10x10_, _12x12_, _14x14_, _16x16_,
_18x18_, _20x20_, _22x22_, _24x24_, _26x26_, _32x32_, _36x36_, _40x40_,
_44x44_, _48x48_, _52x52_, _64x64_, _72x72_, _80x80_, _88x88_, _96x96_,
_104x104_, _120x120_, _132x132_, _144x144_
* If *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder will
default to creating the smallest symbol that holds the data.
* The *c40headerlength* option specifies the number of leading
characters in the data field that must be stored using C40 encodation.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* _Deprecated_: The *format* option is used to specify the shape of the
symbol, either:
** `square` (default)
** `rectangle`: Consider
<<_data_matrix_rectangular,Data Matrix Rectangular>> for rectangular
symbols.
* _Deprecated: Consider
<<_data_matrix_rectangular_extension,Data Matrix Rectangular Extension>>._
The *dmre* option enables Data Matrix Rectangular Extension symbols
based on the ISO/IEC standard, which increases the number of rectangular
symbol sizes available.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, automatically sized, the latter showing use of the
parse option:

....
Data:    This is Data Matrix
Options: 
Encoder: datamatrix
....

....
Data:    This is ^068ata Matrix
Options: parse
Encoder: datamatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNDAiIGhlaWdodD0iNDAiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA0MCA0MCI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

Identical symbols with a fixed size:

....
Data:    Fixed size
Options: version=48x48
Encoder: datamatrix
....

....
Data:    Fixed size
Options: rows=48 columns=48
Encoder: datamatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

An advanced use containing "hidden data" in the padding codewords as
used by some non-standard, "high-security" applications. The technique
works by filling the symbol using raw codewords formed from the standard
data immediately followed by the non-standard padding data beginning
with `^129`:

....
Data:    ^066^067^068^142^052^129^161^056^206^101^251^147
Options: version=16x16 raw
Encoder: datamatrix
....

==== Data Matrix Rectangular

The *Data Matrix Rectangular* symbology is a rectangular variant of
<<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>>.

Uses:

* Marking narrow areas, such as the edge of a part or a narrow label.

Variants:

* <<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> is the standard square variant of the
symbology.
* <<_data_matrix_rectangular_extension,Data Matrix Rectangular Extension>>
is a variant of Data Matrix Rectangular that provides a greater range of
symbol dimensions.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is
useful for specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider
<<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>> for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^PROG`: PROG - Reader programming
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06,
except in a Structured Append symbol.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same
in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one
message from those of another.
** An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the
whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
** FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
** Structured Append is not available with the *raw* option or reader
programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix or
Royal Mail Mailmark symbols.
* When the *dotty* option is specified the modules are rendered as dots
rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the
*inkspread* option.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol.
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC`. Valid options are _8x18_, _8x32_, _12x26_, _12x36_,
_16x36_, _16x48_.
* If *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder will
default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the
given data.
* The *c40headerlength* option specifies the number of leading
characters in the data field that must be stored using C40 encodation.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* _Deprecated: Consider
<<_data_matrix_rectangular_extension,Data Matrix Rectangular Extension>>._
The *dmre* option enables Data Matrix Rectangular Extension symbols
based on the ISO/IEC standard, which increases the number of rectangular
symbol sizes available.

===== Examples

A rectangular symbol with a fixed size:

....
Data:    Rectangular
Options: version=16x48
Encoder: datamatrixrectangular
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

==== Data Matrix Rectangular Extension

The *Data Matrix Rectangular Extension* symbology is an enhancement to
<<_data_matrix_rectangular,Data Matrix Rectangular>> that provides a
greater range of symbol dimensions.

Also known as: DMRE.

Uses:

* Marking narrow areas with more data than a rectangular Data Matrix
holds, where the readers support DMRE (ISO/IEC 21471).

Variants:

* <<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> is the standard square variant of the
symbology.
* <<_data_matrix_rectangular,Data Matrix Rectangular>> is the original
rectangular variant of Data Matrix that provides a limited range of
symbol dimensions.

Standards: ISO/IEC 21471.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is
useful for specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider
<<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>> for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^PROG`: PROG - Reader programming
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06,
except in a Structured Append symbol.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same
in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one
message from those of another.
** An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the
whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
** FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
** Structured Append is not available with the *raw* option or reader
programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix or
Royal Mail Mailmark symbols.
* When the *dotty* option is specified the modules are rendered as dots
rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the
*inkspread* option.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol.
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC`. Valid options are _8x18_, _8x32_, _8x48_, _8x64_, _8x80_,
_8x96_, _8x120_, _8x144_, _12x26_, _12x36_, _12x64_, _12x88_, _16x36_,
_16x48_, _16x64_, _20x36_, _20x44_, _20x64_, _22x48_, _24x48_, _24x64_,
_26x40_, _26x48_, _26x64_.
* If *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder will
default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the
given data.
* The *c40headerlength* option specifies the number of leading

* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level

===== Examples

A DMRE symbol with a fixed size:

....
Data:    1234
Options: version=8x80
Encoder: datamatrixrectangularextension
....

==== Han Xin Code

The *Han Xin Code* symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that
can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Chinese Sensible.

Standards: GB/T 21049-2007.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, `^FNC1` in the first position
of the data selects GS1 mode. FNC1 cannot appear elsewhere.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=L1` - Lowest
** `eclevel=L2` (default)
** `eclevel=L3`
** `eclevel=L4` - Highest
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to
84.
* If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that
is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error
correction level.
* The *mask* option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 4. If
unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.

===== Examples

A fixed-size symbol with maximum error correction:

....
Data:    Han Xin Code
Options: version=10 eclevel=L4
Encoder: hanxin
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iOTQiIGhlaWdodD0iOTQiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA5NCA5NCI{plus}]

==== MicroPDF417

The *MicroPDF417* barcode symbology is 2D stacked-linear barcode based
on <<_pdf417,PDF417>> that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Variants:

* <<_pdf417,PDF417>> is a larger variant of the MicroPDF417 barcode.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC MicroPDF417>> is a variant of MicroPDF417 that
should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24728, AIM ISS - MicroPDF417.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI811799`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>. The symbol is
encoded in Code 128 emulation, which readers report as `++]++C2` or
`++]++L4`. It is not available with *readerinit*, and only in the first
symbol of a Structured Append sequence.
** `^FNC1`: FNC1, a field separator after FNC1 in second position.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in second position.
* Whenever the data field contains suitable input, the encoder will
compress ISO/IEC 15434 structured data (internally using the 05 Macro
and 06 Macro codewords), except in a Structured Append symbol or with
*readerinit*.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol. Valid values, as columns x rows, are:
** _1x11_, _1x14_, _1x17_, _1x20_, _1x24_, _1x28_, _2x8_, _2x11_,
_2x14_, _2x17_, _2x20_, _2x23_, _2x26_, _3x6_, _3x8_, _3x10_, _3x12_,
_3x15_, _3x20_, _3x26_, _3x32_, _3x38_, _3x44_, _4x4_, _4x6_, _4x8_,
_4x10_, _4x12_, _4x15_, _4x20_, _4x26_, _4x32_, _4x38_, _4x44_
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC` (rows first), for example `version=15x4`.
* If the *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder
will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent
the given data.
* The *rowmult* option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with
respect to the minimum module width. The default is 2.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as
the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as
such.
** *samid* is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the
sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to
899, for example `samid=017053`.
** The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender
and time stamp, are not supported.
** Structured Append is not available with the *raw* option or for GS1
Composite symbols.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Structured Append
sequence for reader programming is given it. It is not available with
the *raw* option or for GS1 Composite symbols.
* _Deprecated: Internal use._ The *cca* option identifies this symbol as
a _CC-A_ 2D component of a <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 Composite>>
symbol.
** Special size rules apply when the *cca* option is given, in which
case the *columns* and *rows* options that are used to specify the size
of the symbol must be one of:
*** _2x5_, _2x6_, _2x7_, _2x8_, _2x9_, _2x10_, _2x12_, _3x4_, _3x5_,
_3x6_, _3x7_, _3x8_, _4x3_, _4x4_, _4x5_, _4x6_, _4x7_
* _Deprecated: Internal use._ The *ccb* option identifies this symbol as
a _CC-B_ 2D component of a <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 Composite>>
symbol.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    MicroPDF417
Options:
Encoder: micropdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNDAiIGhlaWdodD0iMzYiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA0MCAzNiI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A symbol using the parse option with fixed dimensions:

....
Data:    MicroP^068F417
Options: parse rows=15 columns=4
Encoder: micropdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

==== PDF417

The *PDF417* barcode symbology is 2D stacked-linear barcode that can
encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Uses:

* North American driver's licences and identity cards (AAMVA DL/ID Card
Design Standard).
* Printed airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
* Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG
B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

* <<_compact_pdf417,Compact PDF417>> is a shortened form of the PDF417
barcode that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is
restricted.
* <<_micropdf417,MicroPDF417>> is a smaller variant of the PDF417
barcode.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC PDF417>> is a variant of PDF417 that should be
used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15438, DD ENV 12925, AIM USS - PDF417.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI811799`: ECI indicators.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level,
from 0 to 8. The default is to choose a standard level of error
correction that is determined by the encoded data length.
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* The *columns* option specifies the number of columns (or groups of
bars) in the output symbol, from 1 to 30.
* The *rows* option specifies the minimum number of rows in the symbol,
from 3 to 90.
* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will select a number that creates
a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
* The *rowmult* option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with
respect to the minimum module width. The default is 3.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Macro PDF417 sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader reassembles
into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as
the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as
such.
** *samid* is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the
sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to
899, for example `samid=017053`.
** The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender
and time stamp, are not supported.
** Macro PDF417 is not available with the *raw* option or for GS1
Composite symbols.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Macro PDF417 sequence
for reader programming is given it. It is not available with the *raw*
option or for GS1 Composite symbols.
* _Deprecated: Use <<_compact_pdf417,Compact PDF417>> instead. The
*compact* option is used to create a compact/truncated PDF417 symbol
that has fewer bars per row than a standard symbol and hence is more
narrow._
* _Deprecated: Internal use._ The *ccc* option identifies this symbol as
a _CC-C_ 2D component of a <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 Composite>>
symbol.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    PDF417
Options:
Encoder: pdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A symbol using the parse option with fixed dimensions:

....
Data:    P^068F417
Options: parse columns=2 rows=15
Encoder: pdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A symbol with increased error correction:

....
Data:    Strong error correction
Options: columns=2 eclevel=5
Encoder: pdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

A symbol using raw codeword input:

....
Data:    ^453^178^121^239
Options: raw columns=2
Encoder: pdf417
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Compact PDF417

*Compact PDF417* is a shortened form of the <<_pdf417,PDF417>> barcode
that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is
restricted.

Also known as: Truncated PDF417.

Variants:

* <<_pdf417,PDF417>> is the larger, more popular variant.
* <<_micropdf417,MicroPDF417>> is a smaller variant of the PDF417
barcode.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC PDF417>> is a variant of PDF417 that should be
used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15438, DD ENV 12925, AIM USS - PDF417.

* The *columns* option specifies the number of columns (or groups of

* The *rows* option specifies the minimum number of rows in the symbol,

* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will select a number that creates

* The *rowmult* option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with
respect to the minimum module width. The default is 3.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samid* options make the symbol one of a
Macro PDF417 sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader reassembles
into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as
the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as
such.
** *samid* is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the
sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to
899, for example `samid=017053`.
** The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender
and time stamp, are not supported.
** Macro PDF417 is not available with the *raw* option.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Macro PDF417 sequence
for reader programming is given it. It is not available with the *raw*
option.

===== Examples

A compact symbol with four columns:

....
Data:    A truncated PDF417
Options: columns=4
Encoder: pdf417compact
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== QR Code

The *QR Code* symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that can
encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Quick Response Code.

Uses:

* Content for phones: web links, Wi-Fi network details, contact cards,
email, phone numbers, text messages, locations and calendar events.
* SEPA credit transfers (<<_epc_qr_code,EPC QR Code>>, also known as
GiroCode).
* Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
* Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU
traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574, with error correction level H.
* Merchant payment QR codes to the EMVCo QR Code Specification, such as
Brazil's Pix (<<_emv_qr_code,EMV QR Code>>).
* Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG
B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

* <<_micro_qr_code,Micro QR Code>> is a small QR Code that is used in
applications that require a small symbol space.
* <<_rectangular_micro_qr_code,Rectangular Micro QR Code>> is a
rectangular variant that provides a compact symbol suitable for narrow,
elongated spaces.
* <<_gs1_qr_code,GS1 QR Code>> is a variant that should be used when
encoding data that is in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* <<_gs1_digital_link_qr_code,GS1 Digital Link QR Code>> is a variant
that should be used when encoding a GS1 Digital Link URI.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC QR Code>> is a variant of QR Code that should be
used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
* <<_swiss_qr_code,Swiss QR Code>> is a variant of the QR Code for use
with the QR-bill application supporting Swiss payments.
* <<_epc_qr_code,EPC QR Code>> is a variant of QR Code carrying the
details of a SEPA credit transfer.
* <<_emv_qr_code,EMV QR Code>> is a variant of QR Code carrying EMV
merchant-presented payment data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, JIS X 0510, ITS - QR Code, AIM ISS - QR Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider <<_gs1_qr_code,GS1 QR Code>>
for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1
mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode
an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=L` - Low
** `eclevel=M` - Medium (default)
** `eclevel=Q` - Quality
** `eclevel=H` - High
** A higher level lets the symbol be read with more of it damaged, such
as by wear or by a logo printed over its centre, at the cost of a larger
symbol. Some applications fix the level, such as M for an EPC QR Code or
a Swiss QR-bill, and H for unit packets of tobacco under Regulation (EU)
2018/574.
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to
40.
* If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that
is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error
correction level.
* The *mask* option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 8. If
unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.
* The *sampos*, *samtotal* and *samparity* options make the symbol one
of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samparity* is the parity of the whole message, from 0 to 255, and is
the same in every symbol of the sequence. It is the XOR of the bytes of
the message, and is reported by the encoder for the data that it encodes
(see
<<_developing_a_frontend_to_bwipp,Developing a Frontend to BWIPP>>), so
the parity of a message is the XOR of the parities reported for its
parts.
** Structured Append is not available for Micro QR Code, Rectangular
Micro QR Code, GS1 QR Code, GS1 Digital Link QR Code, Swiss QR Code, EPC
QR Code or EMV QR Code symbols.
* _Deprecated_: The *suppresskanjimode* option will prevent the use of
Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a
Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the
message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather
than as a data compaction strategy. There's nothing that can be done
other than to disable the use of Kanji Mode data compaction for symbols
intended to be read by such broken readers.
* _Deprecated_: The *format* option is used to specify the symbol type,
either:
** `full` (default)
** `micro`: Consider <<_micro_qr_code,Micro QR Code>> for Micro QR Code
symbols.
** `rmqr`: Consider
<<_rectangular_micro_qr_code,Rectangular Micro QR Code>> for rMQR
symbols.

===== Common Content

Phones recognise the following formats, which are conventions documented
by https://github.com/zxing/zxing/wiki/Barcode-Contents[ZXing] rather
than part of the QR Code standard:

[cols=",",options="header",]
|===
|Content |Data
|Web link |`https://example.com/`

|Wi-Fi network |`WIFI:T:WPA;S:network;P:password;;` with `T` one of
`WEP`, `WPA` (which also serves WPA2 personal networks), `WPA2-EAP` or
`nopass`, and `H:true` added for a hidden network. In the network name
and password, `++\++`, `;`, `,`, `"` and `:` are each preceded by
`++\++`.

|Email |`mailto:someone@example.com`

|Phone number |`tel:{plus}12125551212`

|Text message |`sms:{plus}18005551212:Message` (`SMSTO:` is also seen)

|Location |`geo:40.71872,-73.98905,100` (latitude, longitude and
optionally altitude)

|Contact
|`MECARD:N:Owen,Sean;TEL:12125551212;EMAIL:srowen@example.com;;`, or a
vCard from `BEGIN:VCARD` to `END:VCARD`

|Calendar event |An iCalendar event from `BEGIN:VEVENT` to `END:VEVENT`
|===

The European Payments Council's EPC QR Code, also known as GiroCode,
which initiates a SEPA credit transfer, is available as the
<<_epc_qr_code,EPC QR Code>> variant, which validates its data.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, the latter using the parse option:

....
Data:    QR Code
Options:
Encoder: qrcode
....

....
Data:    QR ^067ode
Options: parse
Encoder: qrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNTgiIGhlaWdodD0iNTgiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA1OCA1OCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjgiIHk9Ii01LjgiIHdpZHRoPSI2OS42IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjY5LjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjgiIHk9Ii01LjgiIHdpZHRoPSI2OS42IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjY5LjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}]

A fixed-size symbol with increased error correction:

....
Data:    QR CODE 1234
Options: version=10 eclevel=Q
Encoder: qrcode
....

==== Micro QR Code

The *Micro QR Code* symbology is a smaller variant of
<<_qr_code,QR Code>> that is used in applications that require a small
symbol space.

Also known as: Micro Quick Response Code.

Uses:

* Small items where a full QR Code does not fit, such as small parts and
electronic components.

Variants:

* <<_qr_code,QR Code>> is the more popular, larger variant.
* <<_rectangular_micro_qr_code,Rectangular Micro QR Code>> is a
rectangular variant that provides a compact symbol suitable for narrow,
elongated spaces.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, JIS X 0510, ITS - QR Code, AIM ISS - QR Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* An appropriate size will be selected to work around the following
restrictions:
** An M1 symbol is only compatible with numeric data.
** An M2 symbol is only compatible with numeric and alphanumeric data.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, either
`version=M1`, `version=M2`, `version=M3` or `version=M4`.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=L` - Low (default)
** `eclevel=M` - Medium; Not compatible with M1 symbols
** `eclevel=Q` - Quality; Only compatible with M4 symbols
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that
is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error
correction level.
* The *mask* option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 4. If
unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.
* _Deprecated_: The *suppresskanjimode* option will prevent the use of
Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a
Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the
message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather
than as a data compaction strategy.

===== Examples

A basic symbol encoding numeric data:

....
Data:    01234567
Options:
Encoder: microqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMzQiIGhlaWdodD0iMzQiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAzNCAzNCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii0zLjQiIHk9Ii0zLjQiIHdpZHRoPSI0MC44IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjQwLjgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii0zLjQiIHk9Ii0zLjQiIHdpZHRoPSI0MC44IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjQwLjgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cg==]

==== Rectangular Micro QR Code

The *Rectangular Micro QR Code* (rMQR) symbology is a rectangular
variant of <<_qr_code,QR Code>> that provides a compact symbol suitable
for applications where a narrow, elongated symbol is required, such as
labels and small cylindrical items.

Also known as: rMQR.

Uses:

* Long, narrow spaces, such as the edges and margins of boxes and
labels.

Variants:

* <<_qr_code,QR Code>> is the more popular, larger square variant.
* <<_micro_qr_code,Micro QR Code>> is a smaller square variant.

Standards: ISO/IEC 23941.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider <<_gs1_qr_code,GS1 QR Code>>
with an `R` version for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1
mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode
an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
* The *version* option is *required* and specifies the size of the
symbol in `RHxW` format, where H is the height and W is the width in
modules:
** R7x43, R7x59, R7x77, R7x99, R7x139
** R9x43, R9x59, R9x77, R9x99, R9x139
** R11x27, R11x43, R11x59, R11x77, R11x99, R11x139
** R13x27, R13x43, R13x59, R13x77, R13x99, R13x139
** R15x43, R15x59, R15x77, R15x99, R15x139
** R17x43, R17x59, R17x77, R17x99, R17x139
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=M` - Medium (default)
** `eclevel=H` - High
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the selected symbol
is possible.
* _Deprecated_: The *suppresskanjimode* option will prevent the use of
Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a
Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the
message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather
than as a data compaction strategy.

===== Examples

A numeric-only symbol:

....
Data:    1234
Options: version=R17x139
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A Figure 1 example symbol from the specification:

....
Data:    12345678901234567890123456
Options: version=R13x27 eclevel=M fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNjIiIGhlaWdodD0iMzQiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA2MiAzNCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii02LjIiIHk9Ii0zLjQiIHdpZHRoPSI3NC40IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjQwLjgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii02LjIiIHk9Ii0zLjQiIHdpZHRoPSI3NC40IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjQwLjgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cg==]

An alphanumeric symbol:

....
Data:    AC-42
Options: version=R7x59 eclevel=H fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A symbol with ECI:

....
Data:    ^ECI000009^161^162^163^164^165
Options: parse parsefnc version=R17x139 eclevel=M fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode
....

==== Swiss QR Code

*Swiss QR Code* is a variant of the <<_qr_code,QR Code>> barcode
symbology for use with the QR-bill application supporting Swiss
payments.

Uses:

* Swiss and Liechtenstein payment slips (QR-bill).

Standards: Swiss Implementation Guidelines QR-bill, ISO/IEC 18004, ITS -
QR Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in the format described in the Swiss
Implementation Guidelines QR-bill document.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol. This
is not typically specified.
* If the *version* is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a
symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at error
correction level M, which the Swiss Implementation Guidelines require.
* _Deprecated_: The *suppresskanjimode* option will prevent the use of
Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a
Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the
message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather
than as a data compaction strategy.

Note: The symbol is drawn 46mm x 46mm, excluding the quiet zone,
whatever its version, with a 7mm x 7mm Swiss Cross over its centre.

===== Examples

A QR-bill payment with structured creditor reference:

....
Data:    SPC^010\
         0200^010\
         1^010\
         CH5800791123000889012^010\
         S^010\
         Robert Schneider AG^010\
         Rue du Lac^010\
         1268^010\
         2501^010\
         Biel^010\
         CH^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         199.95^010\
         CHF^010\
         S^010\
         Pia-Maria Rutschmann-Schnyder^010\
         Grosse Marktgasse^010\
         28^010\
         9400^010\
         Rorschach^010\
         CH^010\
         SCOR^010\
         RF18539007547034^010\
         ^010\
         EPD
Options: parse
Encoder: swissqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii0xMy4xIiB5PSItMTMuMSIgd2lkdGg9IjE1Ny4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjE1Ny4yIiBmaWxsPSJyZ2IoMTAwJSwgMTAwJSwgMTAwJSkiIGZpbGwtb3BhY2l0eT0iMSIvPgo8ZyBjbGlwLXBhdGg9InVybCgjY2xpcC0wKSI{plus}{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== EPC QR Code

*EPC QR Code* is a variant of the <<_qr_code,QR Code>> barcode symbology
carrying the details of a SEPA credit transfer, so that a payer can
initiate the payment by scanning it, for example from an invoice. It is
also known as the GiroCode.

Uses:

* Payments in euro across the Single Euro Payments Area.

Standards: EPC069-12 Quick Response Code - Guidelines to Enable the Data
Capture for the Initiation of a SEPA Credit Transfer, ISO/IEC 18004, ITS
- QR Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is the payload described in the EPC guidelines:
up to 12 elements separated by line feeds (or carriage return and line
feed), in this order, with nothing after the last element given:
** Service Tag, `BCD`.
** Version, `001` or `002`.
** Character set of the elements that follow: `1` UTF-8, `2` ISO 8859-1,
`3` ISO 8859-2, `4` ISO 8859-4, `5` ISO 8859-5, `6` ISO 8859-7, `7` ISO
8859-10, `8` ISO 8859-15.
** Identification, `SCT`.
** The BIC of the beneficiary's bank, of 8 or 11 characters, which may
be empty in version `002`.
** The name of the beneficiary, up to 70 characters.
** The IBAN of the beneficiary's account.
** Optionally the amount: `EUR` followed by an amount from 0.01 to
999999999.99.
** Optionally the purpose: a code of up to 4 characters.
** Optionally either a structured creditor reference of up to 35
characters, such as an ISO 11649 `RF` reference, or remittance text of
up to 140 characters, but not both.
** Optionally information for the payer, up to 70 characters.
* The encoder validates the elements, including the check digits of the
IBAN and of an `RF` creditor reference. The whole payload must not
exceed 331 bytes.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying the line feeds as `^010` and other characters.
* The symbol is created at error correction level M, which the EPC
guidelines require.

===== Examples

A payment with an amount and a structured creditor reference:

....
Data:    BCD^010\
         001^010\
         1^010\
         SCT^010\
         BHBLDEHHXXX^010\
         Franz Mustermann^010\
         DE71110220330123456789^010\
         EUR12.3^010\
         GDDS^010\
         RF18539007547034
Options: parse
Encoder: epcqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iOTAiIGhlaWdodD0iOTAiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA5MCA5MCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii05IiB5PSItOSIgd2lkdGg9IjEwOCIgaGVpZ2h0PSIxMDgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii05IiB5PSItOSIgd2lkdGg9IjEwOCIgaGVpZ2h0PSIxMDgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A version 002 payment without a BIC, with information for the payer:

....
Data:    BCD^010\
         002^010\
         1^010\
         SCT^010\
         ^010\
         Harbour Choir^010\
         DE89370400440532013000^010\
         EUR12.50^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         Donation
Options: parse
Encoder: epcqrcode
....
