==== EMV QR Code

*EMV QR Code* is a variant of the <<_qr_code,QR Code>> barcode symbology
that carries the merchant-presented payment data of the EMV QR Code
Specification for Payment Systems, which is the basis of national
payment QR codes such as Pix (Brazil), Bharat QR (India), PayNow
(Singapore), PromptPay (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), QRIS (Indonesia)
and KE-QR (Kenya).

Uses:

* Payment QR codes presented by merchants at the point of sale, under
national schemes such as Pix, Bharat QR, PayNow, PromptPay, DuitNow,
QRIS and KE-QR.

Standards: EMV QR Code Specification for Payment Systems (EMV QRCPS) -
Merchant-Presented Mode; ISO/IEC 18004.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the payload of data objects, each a two-digit ID, a
two-digit length and a value of that many characters, beginning with the
Payload Format Indicator `000201` and ending with the CRC object `6304`
and its four upper case hexadecimal digits.
* If the CRC object is omitted then the encoder will calculate and add
it. If it is given then it is verified.
* The encoder validates the data objects of the specification:
** Each ID appears at most once, and IDs 65 to 79 are reserved.
** At least one Merchant Account Information object, IDs 02 to 51, is
present, and the templates 26 to 51 and 80 to 99 begin with a Globally
Unique Identifier.
** The Merchant Category Code (52), Transaction Currency (53), Country
Code (58), Merchant Name (59) and Merchant City (60) are present and
well formed.
** The Point of Initiation Method (01), Transaction Amount (54), Tip or
Convenience Indicator with its fixed or percentage fee (55 to 57),
Postal Code (61), Additional Data Field Template (62) and Merchant
Information Language Template (64) are well formed when present.
* The alternate language template may contain UTF-8 text, whose lengths
count characters.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent byte value.
* The options of <<_qr_code,QR Code>>, such as *eclevel*, are available,
except for Structured Append.

===== Examples

A static merchant code, with the CRC calculated by the encoder:

....
Data:    00020101021126310015COM.EXAMPLE.PAY0108123456785204581253038405802US5913CORNER BAKERY6009SPRINGTON
Options:
Encoder: emvqrcode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iOTAiIGhlaWdodD0iOTAiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA5MCA5MCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii05IiB5PSItOSIgd2lkdGg9IjEwOCIgaGVpZ2h0PSIxMDgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii05IiB5PSItOSIgd2lkdGg9IjEwOCIgaGVpZ2h0PSIxMDgiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cg==]

=== One-Dimensional

==== Code 128

*Code 128* is an arbitrarily long, high-density barcode symbology that
can be used to encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: USD-6, USS-128, Code 128A, Code 128B, Code 128C.

Uses:

* Identifiers outside the GS1 system, such as carrier tracking numbers
and warehouse, bin, inventory and asset labels.
* Amazon FNSKU product labels.
* Aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability
Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
* Blood, tissue and cell products labelled to ISBT 128.
* International registered mail, parcels and EMS, carrying the
<<_upu_s10,UPU S10>> tracking number.
* DPD parcel labels (<<_dpd_parcel_label,DPD Parcel Label>>).
* Clinical laboratory specimen tubes (CLSI AUTO02).
* Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG
B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

* <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>> is a variant of Code 128 that should be used when
encoding data that is in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC Code 128>> is a variant of Code 128 that should
be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
* <<_upu_s10,UPU S10>> is a variant of Code 128 carrying the S10
identifier of a postal item.
* <<_dpd_parcel_label,DPD Parcel Label>> is a variant of Code 128 on the
parcel labels of DPD.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4 - ISS Code 128, BS EN 799.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII or extended-ASCII
value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. `^029` for
_GS_, `^209` for _Ñ_, etc.
* _FNC4_ function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the
encoding of extended ASCII characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>> for
encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>. The human readable
text leaves out this FNC1.
** `^FNC2`: FNC2
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
* _Deprecated:_ The *raw* option denotes that the data field is
providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable
for direct low-level encoding. You can use the *alttext* option to
specify human-readable text.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ When the *parsefnc* option is
specified, the special pseudo characters `^LNKA` and `^LNKC` at the end
of the symbol indicate that a GS1-128 symbol includes a _CC-A/B_ or
_CC-C_ GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

A symbol encoding alphanumeric data:

....
Data:    Count0123456789!
Options: includetext
Encoder: code128
....

==== Code 39

The *Code 39* barcode symbology is discrete, variable length and
self-checking.

Also known as: Code 3 of 9, Alpha39, USD-3, USS-39.

Uses:

* Asset and inventory labels.
* US military shipping labels and container markings
(<<_logmars,LOGMARS>>, MIL-STD-129).
* Vehicle Identification Numbers (<<_vin,VIN>>).
* Automotive trading-partner labels (AIAG B-10), each field carrying its
Data Identifier.
* European automotive goods labels (Odette Transport Label, VDA 4902).

Variants:

* <<_code_39_extended,Code 39 Extended>> is a variant of Code 39 that
can be used to encode full 128 character ASCII with the use of shift
character combinations.
* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC Code 39>> is a variant of Code 39 that should be
used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
* <<_logmars,LOGMARS>> is the use of Code 39 by the US Department of
Defense.
* <<_vin,VIN>> is a variant of Code 39 carrying a Vehicle Identification
Number.
* <<_codablock_a,Codablock A>> is a stacked symbology whose rows are
Code 39 symbols.
* AIM USD-2 is a subset of Code 39 containing the characters A-Z, 0-9,
_space_, `-` and `.`.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16388, ANSI/AIM BC1 - USS Code 39, BS EN 800,
MIL-STD-1189.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can hold any of the following:
** Numbers 0-9
** Capital letters A-Z
** Symbols `-.$/{plus}%` and _space_
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character of the data to be
the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digit
appear in the human readable text.
* The *hidestars* option suppresses the asterisks in the human readable
text.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    CODE39
Options: includetext
Encoder: code39
....

A symbol with a check digit:

Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: code39
....

==== Code 39 Extended

The *Code 39 Extended* barcode symbology is discrete, variable length
and self-checking. It is based on <<_code_39,Code 39>> but can encode
full 128 character ASCII by using shift combinations.

Also known as: Code 39 Full ASCII.

Uses:

* Code 39 labels that need lowercase letters or other ASCII characters,
read by scanners set to Full ASCII.

Variants:

* <<_code_39,Code 39>> is a simpler variant of Code 39 Extended.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16388, ANSI/AIM BC1 - USS Code 39, BS EN 800.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any ASCII data.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters, e.g. `^029` for _GS_, etc.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character of the data to be
the check character, calculated over the shift-encoded Code 39
characters, and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digit
appear in the human readable text.
* The *hidestars* option suppresses the asterisks in the human readable
text.

===== Examples

A symbol encoding lowercase and special characters:

....
Data:    Code39 Ext!
Options: includetext includecheck
Encoder: code39ext
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMzM5IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMzM5IDgwIj4KPGRlZnM{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNSI{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtOCI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtOSI{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZGVmcz4KPHJlY3QgeD0iLTMzLjkiIHk9Ii04IiB3aWR0aD0iNDA2LjgiIGhlaWdodD0iOTYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtMiIgeD0iMTI0LjUiIHk9Ijc5LjE1NzgxMiIvPgo8dXNlIHhsaW5rOmhyZWY9IiNnbHlwaC0wLTMiIHg9IjEzMC41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC00IiB4PSIxMzYuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtMyIgeD0iMTQyLjUiIHk9Ijc5LjE1NzgxMiIvPgo8dXNlIHhsaW5rOmhyZWY9IiNnbHlwaC0wLTUiIHg9IjE0OC41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC0zIiB4PSIxNTQuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtNiIgeD0iMTYwLjUiIHk9Ijc5LjE1NzgxMiIvPgo8dXNlIHhsaW5rOmhyZWY9IiNnbHlwaC0wLTciIHg9IjE2Ni41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC0zIiB4PSIxNzIuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtOCIgeD0iMTc4LjUiIHk9Ijc5LjE1NzgxMiIvPgo8dXNlIHhsaW5rOmhyZWY9IiNnbHlwaC0wLTkiIHg9IjE4NC41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC0zIiB4PSIxOTAuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtMTAiIHg9IjE5Ni41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC0zIiB4PSIyMDIuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtMTEiIHg9IjIwOC41IiB5PSI3OS4xNTc4MTIiLz4KPHVzZSB4bGluazpocmVmPSIjZ2x5cGgtMC0zIiB4PSIyMTQuNSIgeT0iNzkuMTU3ODEyIi8{plus}Cjx1c2UgeGxpbms6aHJlZj0iI2dseXBoLTAtMCIgeD0iMjIwLjUiIHk9Ijc5LjE1NzgxMiIvPgo8L2c{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Code 93

*Code 93* is a continuous, variable length, self-checking barcode
symbology.

Also known as: USD-7, USS-93.

Variants:

* <<_code_93_extended,Code 93 Extended>> is a variant of Code 93 that
can be used to encode full 128 character ASCII with the use of special
shift character combinations.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC5 - USS Code 93, ITS 93i.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can hold any of the following:
** Numbers 0-9
** Capital letters A-Z
** Symbols `-.$/{plus}%` and _space_
* The *includecheck* option calculates the two check digits.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last two characters of the data
to be the check characters C and K and refuses the data if they are
wrong. A check character that is a shift character is given as `^SFT$`,
`^SFT%`, `^SFT/` or `^SFT{plus}` with *parsefnc*.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *parsefnc* option allows the
special shift characters to be supplied as escape sequences:
** `^SFT$`: ($)
** `^SFT%`: (%)
** `^SFT/`: (/)
** `^SFT{plus}`: ({plus})

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    CODE93
Options: includecheck
Encoder: code93
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A symbol including a special shift combination `(/)A` representing _!_:

....
Data:    CODE93^SFT/A
Options: parsefnc includecheck
Encoder: code93
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

==== Code 93 Extended

The *Code 93 Extended* barcode symbology is continuous, variable length
and self-checking. It is based on <<_code_93,Code 93>> but can encode
full 128 character ASCII using four additional shift characters: _($)_
_(%)_ _(/)_ _({plus})_

Also known as: Code 93 Full ASCII.

Variants:

* <<_code_93,Code 93>> is a simpler variant of the Code 93 Extended
barcode symbology.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC5 - USS Code 93, ITS 93i.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any ASCII data.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters, e.g. `^029` for _GS_, etc.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the two check digits.
* The *validatecheck* option is not available, since the check
characters need not be ASCII characters.

===== Examples

A symbol encoding lowercase and special characters:

....
Data:    Code93Ext!
Options: includecheck
Encoder: code93ext
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A symbol using the parse option to encode a _GS_ control character:

....
Data:    Code93^029Extended
Options: parse includecheck
Encoder: code93ext
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

==== Interleaved 2 of 5

*Interleaved 2 of 5* is a high-density numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: ITF, Code 2 of 5 Interleaved, USD-1, USS-Interleaved 2 of
5.

Uses:

* Brazilian bank payment slips (boleto bancário), carrying the 44-digit
payment code.
* Numeric identifiers on cartons and in warehousing; for the GTIN of a
case, <<_itf_14,ITF-14>> is its GS1 form.

Variants:

* <<_itf_14,ITF-14>> is a variant of Interleaved 2 of 5 that should be
used when encoding a fourteen-digit GTIN.
* <<_deutsche_post_identcode,Deutsche Post Identcode>> is a variant of
Interleaved 2 of 5 that is used by Deutsche Post to identify parcels.
* <<_deutsche_post_leitcode,Deutsche Post Leitcode>> is a variant of
Interleaved 2 of 5 that is used by Deutsche Post to carry a parcel's
routing code.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16390, ANSI/AIM BC2 - USS Interleaved 2 of 5, BS EN
801.

===== Data and Options

* The data can consist of any number of digits.
* If the length of the symbol including the possible check digit would
be odd then the data is prefixed by _0_.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated checksum appear
in the human readable text.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    0123456789
Options:
Encoder: interleaved2of5
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

A symbol with a check digit:

....
Data:    2401234567
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: interleaved2of5
....

=== Supply Chain

==== EAN-14

*EAN-14* is an implementation of the <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>> barcode
symbology with _AI (01)_ that is used to encode a lone GTIN-14.

Note: EAN-14 is a colloquial term used to describe a GS1-128 barcode
symbol containing only a GTIN.

Also known as: GS1-128 without attribute data.

Misnomers: UCC-14.

Uses:

* The GTIN of a trade item grouping, such as a case or carton, alone on
a GS1 logistic label.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. `(01)...`.
* Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human
readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
* If thirteen digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* With *strictspec*, the *ast* option takes the <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>>
application standards, such as `ast=gs1.sst2` for trade items scanned in
general distribution.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)09528765432108
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean14
....

....
Data:    (01)0952876543210
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean14
....

==== ITF-14

*ITF-14* is an implementation of the
<<_interleaved_2_of_5,Interleaved 2 of 5>> barcode symbology that is
typically used to encode a GTIN-14, GTIN-13 or GTIN-12.

Also known as: UPC Shipping Container Symbol, SCS, UPC Case Code.

Uses:

* The GTIN of outer cases and cartons of trade items in distribution,
often printed directly onto corrugated board.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16390, ANSI/AIM BC2 - USS Interleaved 2 of 5, BS EN
801, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of either thirteen or fourteen digits.
* Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human
readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
* If thirteen digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated
automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
* A bearer frame surrounding the symbol and its quiet zones is drawn by
default (*showborder*). The GS1 General Specifications require one, with
a nominal thickness of 4.83 mm, when the symbol is printed using
printing plates, typically directly onto corrugated board. The
*borderwidth* option sets its thickness.
* The *showbearer* option draws bearer bars at the top and bottom only,
in place of the frame, as allowed when the symbol is printed without
printing plates.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    09528765432108
Options: includetext
Encoder: itf14
....

....
Data:    0952876543210
Options: includetext
Encoder: itf14
....

==== SSCC-18

*SSCC-18* is an implementation of the <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>> barcode
symbology with _AI (00)_ that is typically used to encode a lone
eighteen-digit shipping container serial number.

Note: SSCC-18 is a colloquial term used to describe a GS1-128 barcode
symbol containing only an SSCC.

Also known as: NVE.

Misnomers: EAN-18.

Uses:

* The SSCC alone on the logistic (shipping) label of a pallet or other
logistic unit.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (00)_ with seventeen or
eighteen digits of a Serial Shipping Container Code, i.e. `(00)...`.
* Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human
readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
* If seventeen digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* With *strictspec*, the *ast* option takes the <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>>
application standards, such as `ast=gs1.sst5` for a logistic label.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (00)095287654321012346
Options: includetext
Encoder: sscc18
....

....
Data:    (00)09528765432101234
Options: includetext
Encoder: sscc18
....

==== GS1 DataMatrix

*GS1 DataMatrix* is an implementation of the
<<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> (ECC 200) barcode symbology with
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 formatted>> data.

Uses:

* Healthcare: human and veterinary pharmaceutical (drug) packs
(including the EU Falsified Medicines Directive and the US Drug Supply
Chain Security Act) and medical devices (UDI).
* Direct part marking, such as by laser, chemical etching or dot peen.
* Retail point of sale in 2D, one of the symbols that GS1 US's
https://www.gs1us.org/industries-and-insights/by-topic/sunrise-2027[Sunrise
2027] initiative aims for scanners to read.
* Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU
traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
* Patient wristbands and staff identification in hospitals (GSRN).
* Logistic (shipping) labels, beside the GS1-128 barcode or alone on
small logistic units.
* Returnable and individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).

Variants:

* <<_gs1_datamatrix_rectangular,GS1 DataMatrix Rectangular>> is
equivalent to using `format=rectangle`.
* <<_gs1_digital_link_data_matrix,GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix>> encodes
GS1 data as a Digital Link URI.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* The *format* option is used to specify the shape of the symbol, either
`square` (default) or `rectangle`.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol.
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC`. Valid options are:
** With `format=square`: _10x10_, _12x12_, _14x14_, _16x16_, _18x18_,
_20x20_, _22x22_, _24x24_, _26x26_, _32x32_, _36x36_, _40x40_, _44x44_,
_48x48_, _52x52_, _64x64_, _72x72_, _80x80_, _88x88_, _96x96_,
_104x104_, _120x120_, _132x132_, _144x144_
** With `format=rectangle`: _8x18_, _8x32_, _12x26_, _12x36_, _16x36_,
_16x48_
* If *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder will
default to creating a symbol of the specified *format* that is the
minimum size to represent the given data.
* With *strictspec*, the *ast* option sizes the symbol to a GS1
application standard, such as:
** `ast=gs1.sst6` - healthcare primary packaging, such as a blister or
vial
** `ast=gs1.sst8` - healthcare packs also scanned in general
distribution
** `ast=gs1.sst10` - healthcare packs dispensed to the patient, such as
an outer pack carrying the EU Falsified Medicines Directive's unique
identifier
** `ast=gs1.sst7.dpm.a` - direct part marking with a connected finder
pattern, such as by laser or chemical etching
** `ast=gs1.sst7.dpm.b` - direct part marking with separate modules,
such as by dot peen
** `ast=gs1.sst12.trade`, `ast=gs1.sst12.group` - tobacco unit packets,
and aggregated packaging

===== Examples

GTIN _9521234543213_; Weight _0.123kg_:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options:
Encoder: gs1datamatrix
....

==== GS1 QR Code

*GS1 QR Code* is an implementation of the <<_qr_code,QR Code>> barcode
symbology with
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 formatted data>>.

Uses:

* Logistic (shipping) labels, beside the GS1-128 barcode or alone on
small logistic units.
* Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU
traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
* Returnable and individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).
* Direct part marking of items other than medical devices.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_digital_link_qr_code,GS1 Digital Link QR Code>> encodes GS1
data as a Digital Link URI.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=L` - Low
** `eclevel=M` - Medium (default)
** `eclevel=Q` - Quality
** `eclevel=H` - High
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to
40.
* If the *version* is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a
symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the
selected error correction level.
* With *strictspec*, the *ast* option sizes the symbol to a GS1
application standard, such as `ast=gs1.sst12.trade` for tobacco unit
packets (with `eclevel=H`) and `ast=gs1.sst12.group` for aggregated
packaging.

===== Examples

GTIN _9521234543213_; Extended packaging URL:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213(8200)http://www.abc.net
Options:
Encoder: gs1qrcode
....

==== GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix

*GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix* is an implementation of the
<<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> (ECC 200) barcode symbology containing a
GS1 Digital Link URI.

Uses:

* Products whose 2D code a point-of-sale scanner reads for the GTIN and
a phone opens as a web page (GS1 Digital Link).

Variants:

* <<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>> encodes GS1 data in Application
Identifier format.

Data syntax: GS1 Digital Link URI.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix, GS1 Digital
Link Standard: URI Syntax.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided as a GS1 Digital Link URI.
* The *includetext* option enables the display of HRI.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* The *format* option is used to specify the shape of the symbol, either
`square` (default) or `rectangle`.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol.
* The *version* option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as
`version=RxC`. Valid options are:
** With `format=square`: _10x10_, _12x12_, _14x14_, _16x16_, _18x18_,
_20x20_, _22x22_, _24x24_, _26x26_, _32x32_, _36x36_, _40x40_, _44x44_,
_48x48_, _52x52_, _64x64_, _72x72_, _80x80_, _88x88_, _96x96_,
_104x104_, _120x120_, _132x132_, _144x144_
** With `format=rectangle`: _8x18_, _8x32_, _12x26_, _12x36_, _16x36_,
_16x48_
* If *columns*, *rows* and *version* are unspecified the encoder will
default to creating a symbol of the specified *format* that is the
minimum size to represent the given data.

===== Examples

A GS1 Digital Link URI containing GTIN and additional data:

....
Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options:
Encoder: gs1dldatamatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNjgiIGhlaWdodD0iNjgiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA2OCA2OCI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii02LjgiIHk9Ii02LjgiIHdpZHRoPSI4MS42IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgxLjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii02LjgiIHk9Ii02LjgiIHdpZHRoPSI4MS42IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgxLjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

With human readable interpretation:

....
Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options: includetext

==== GS1 Digital Link QR Code

*GS1 Digital Link QR Code* is an implementation of the
<<_qr_code,QR Code>> barcode symbology containing a GS1 Digital Link
URI.

Uses:

* Retail product packaging that a phone opens as a web page and a 2D
point-of-sale scanner reads for the GTIN, one of the symbols that GS1
US's
https://www.gs1us.org/industries-and-insights/by-topic/sunrise-2027[Sunrise
2027] initiative aims for scanners to read. Until they do, products
usually also carry their EAN/UPC barcode.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_qr_code,GS1 QR Code>> encodes GS1 data in Application
Identifier format.

Data syntax: GS1 Digital Link URI.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code, GS1 Digital Link Standard: URI
Syntax.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided as a GS1 Digital Link URI.
* The *includetext* option enables the display of HRI.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=L` - Low
** `eclevel=M` - Medium (default)
** `eclevel=Q` - Quality
** `eclevel=H` - High
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to
40.
* If the *version* is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a
symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the
selected error correction level.

===== Examples

A GS1 Digital Link URI containing GTIN and additional data:

....
Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options:
Encoder: gs1dlqrcode
....

==== GS1-128

*GS1-128* is an implementation of the <<_code_128,Code 128>> barcode
symbology which carries
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 formatted>> data.

Also known as: UCC/EAN-128, EAN-128, UCC-128.

Uses:

* GS1 logistic labels (shipping labels) on pallets, cases and other
logistic units, carrying the SSCC and data such as batch or lot numbers,
dates and weights.
* Aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability
Regulation (EU) 2018/574 (GS1 SST 12).
* Cases and cartons in distribution carrying a batch, an expiry or
best-before date, or a weight with the GTIN.
* Healthcare: pharmaceutical packs and medical devices, including UDI
labels.
* Returnable assets such as kegs, gas cylinders, pallets and crates, and
individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).

Variants:

* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1-128 Composite>> is a variant of GS1-128
that should be used when a CC-A, CC-B or CC-C GS1 composite 2D component
is required.
* <<_ean_14,EAN-14>> is a variant of GS1-128 that should be used when
encoding a lone fourteen-digit GTIN.
* <<_sscc_18,SSCC-18>> is a variant of GS1-128 that should be used when
encoding a lone eighteen-digit SSCC.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General
Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkagea* option specifies that
the symbol includes a _CC-A_ or _CC-B_ GS1 composite 2D component.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkagec* option specifies that
the symbol includes a _CC-C_ GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

GTIN _9521234543213_; Weight _0.123kg_:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options: includetext
Encoder: gs1-128
....

==== GS1 DotCode

*GS1 DotCode* is an implementation of the <<_dotcode,DotCode>> barcode
symbology with
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 formatted>> data.

Uses:

* Unit packets of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU)
2018/574.

Variants:

* <<_dotcode,DotCode>> is the base symbology without GS1-specific
formatting.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: AIM - ISS DotCode, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* The *ratio* option is used to specify the aspect ratio of the symbol.
The default is 1.5.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol. When these are not specified a symbol is generated that
maintains the selected aspect ratio.
* With *strictspec*, the *ast* option sizes the symbol to a GS1
application standard, such as `ast=gs1.sst12.trade` for tobacco unit
packets.
* _Deprecated: Use only if performance is a concern._ The *fast* option
is used to enable the optional high-speed symbol masking algorithm.

===== Examples

TPX _5vBZIF%!++<++B;?oa%_; GTIN _9521234543213_; Production date/time:

....
Data:    (235)5vBZIF%!<B;?oa%(01)09521234543213(8008)19052001
Options: rows=16
Encoder: gs1dotcode
....

=== GS1 DataBar Family

==== GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional

*GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional* is a fixed-length, linear barcode
symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14.

Uses:

* Small retail items scanned at point of sale, such as loose fresh
produce.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_stacked_omnidirectional,GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional>>
is a variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional for use where a taller,
narrower symbol is required.
* <<_gs1_databar_truncated,GS1 DataBar Truncated>> is a variant of GS1
DataBar Omnidirectional of reduced height for items not scanned at point
of sale.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional Composite>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional that should be used when a CC-A
or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. `(01)...`.
* If thirteen digits of _AI (01)_ data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databaromni
....

....
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databaromni
....

==== GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional

*GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional* is a fixed-length, stacked linear
barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 for use at point
of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Stacked Omnidirectional.

Uses:

* Small retail items scanned at point of sale, such as loose fruit and
vegetables.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_omnidirectional,GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional for use where a shorter,
wider symbol is required.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional Composite>>
is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional that should be used
when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. `(01)...`.
* If thirteen digits of _AI (01)_ data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* The *barxmult* option specifies the height of each row in modules, at
least _33_. The default is _33_.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)24012345678905
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedomni
....

....
Data:    (01)2401234567890
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedomni
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNTAiIGhlaWdodD0iNjkiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA1MCA2OSI{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== GS1 DataBar Expanded

*GS1 DataBar Expanded* is a variable-length, linear barcode symbology
that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 alongside a number of other
application identifiers for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Expanded.

Uses:

* Fresh and variable-measure products scanned at point of sale, carrying
a weight, price, expiry date or batch with the GTIN.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_expanded_stacked,GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded for use where a taller, narrower symbol
is required.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Expanded Composite>> is a variant
of GS1 DataBar Expanded that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1
composite 2D component is required.
* <<_gs1_north_american_coupon_code,GS1 North American Coupon Code>> is
an application of GS1 DataBar Expanded for manufacturer coupons in the
US and Canada.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* If the data contains a number of application identifiers matching any
of the specifications below then they should be provided in this given
order for maximum encoding efficiency:
** `(01)9...(3103)...` (this and the next four only when no other AIs
follow)
** `(01)9...(3202)...`
** `(01)9...(3203)...`
** `(01)9...(310x/320x)...(11/13/15/17)...`
** `(01)9...(310x/320x)...`
** `(01)9...(392x)...`
** `(01)9...(393x)...`
** `(01)...`
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

GTIN _9521234543213_; Weight _0.123kg_:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options:
Encoder: databarexpanded
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

==== GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked

*GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked* is a variable-length, stacked-linear
barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 alongside a
number of other application identifiers for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Expanded Stacked.

Uses:

* Fresh and variable-measure products scanned at point of sale whose
packaging is too narrow for GS1 DataBar Expanded, carrying a weight,
price, expiry date or batch with the GTIN.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_expanded,GS1 DataBar Expanded>> is a variant of GS1
DataBar Expanded Stacked for use where a shorter, wider symbol is
required.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked Composite>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked that should be used when a CC-A
or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.
* <<_gs1_north_american_coupon_code,GS1 North American Coupon Code>> is
an application of GS1 DataBar Expanded for manufacturer coupons in the
US and Canada.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* If the data contains a number of application identifiers matching any
of the specifications below then they should be provided in this given
order for maximum encoding efficiency:
** `(01)9...(3103)...` (this and the next four only when no other AIs
follow)
** `(01)9...(3202)...`
** `(01)9...(3203)...`
** `(01)9...(310x/320x)...(11/13/15/17)...`
** `(01)9...(310x/320x)...`
** `(01)9...(392x)...`
** `(01)9...(393x)...`
** `(01)...`
* The *segments* option is used to specify the maximum number of
segments per row, an even number from _2_ to _22_. The default is _4_.
* The *barxmult* option specifies the height of each row in modules, at
least _34_. The default is _34_.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

GTIN _9521234543213_; Weight _0.123kg_:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options: segments=4
Encoder: databarexpandedstacked
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== GS1 DataBar Truncated

*GS1 DataBar Truncated* is a fixed-length, linear barcode symbology that
can be used to encode a GTIN-14 on items not scanned at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Truncated.

Uses:

* Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_stacked,GS1 DataBar Stacked>> is a variant of GS1
DataBar Truncated for use where a taller, narrower symbol is required.
* <<_gs1_databar_omnidirectional,GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated of full height for items scanned at
point of sale.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Truncated Composite>> is a
variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B
GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. `(01)...`.
* If thirteen digits of _AI (01)_ data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databartruncated
....

....
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databartruncated
....

==== GS1 DataBar Stacked

*GS1 DataBar Stacked* is a fixed-length, stacked linear barcode
symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 on items not scanned at
point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Stacked.

Uses:

* Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_databar_truncated,GS1 DataBar Truncated>> is a variant of GS1
DataBar Stacked for use where a shorter, wider symbol is required.
* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Stacked Composite>> is a variant
of GS1 DataBar Stacked that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1
composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. `(01)...`.
* If thirteen digits of _AI (01)_ data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databarstacked
....

....
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databarstacked
....

==== GS1 DataBar Limited

*GS1 DataBar Limited* is a fixed-length, linear barcode symbology that
can be used to encode a GTIN-14 beginning with _0_ or _1_ on items not
scanned at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Limited.

Uses:

* Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 DataBar Limited Composite>> is a variant
of GS1 DataBar Limited that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1
composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS -
Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input must be a solitary _AI (01)_ with thirteen or
fourteen digits of a GTIN starting with _0_ or _1_, i.e. `(01)0...` or
`(01)1...`.
* If thirteen digits of _AI (01)_ data are supplied then the check digit
is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be
verified.
* _Deprecated: For internal use._ The *linkage* option signifies the
presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databarlimited
....

....
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databarlimited
....

==== GS1 North American Coupon Code

*GS1 North American Coupon Code* is an implementation of the
<<_gs1_databar_expanded,GS1 DataBar Expanded>> barcode symbology with AI
(8110) that is used for paper manufacturer coupons at point of sale.

Also known as: GS1 DataBar Coupon, U.S. Coupon Code.

Uses:

* Manufacturer coupons redeemed at point of sale in the US and Canada,
which replaced the UPC prefix 5 coupons.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: North American Coupon Application Guideline Using GS1 DataBar
Expanded Symbols, ISO/IEC 24724, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input is provided in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>
and must be a solitary AI (8110).
* The *includetext* option shows the GS1 Company Prefix and Offer Code,
separated by a dash, above the symbol.
* The *segments* option is used to specify the maximum number of
segments per row which must be an even number. The default is _4_.
* The following options control the placement and styling of the coupon
text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding
`text1++*++` option (see <<_text_properties,Text Properties>>):
** *coupontext*: Override the coupon label content
** *coupontextfont*: PostScript font name for text above symbol
** *coupontextsize*: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
** *coupontextcolor*: Colour for the text above symbol
** *coupontextxalign*, *coupontextyalign*: Alignment of the text above
symbol
** *coupontextxoffset*, *coupontextyoffset*: Position of the text above
symbol, in points
** *coupontextdirection*: Direction of the text above symbol
** *coupontextgaps*: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in
points
** *coupontextsubspace*, *coupontextsplit*, *coupontextlinegaps*:
Multi-line text formatting

===== Examples

A coupon code with eight segments per row:

....
Data:    (8110)106141416543213500110000310123196000
Options: includetext segments=8
Encoder: gs1northamericancoupon
....

=== Postal Symbols

==== Australia Post 4 State Customer Code

The *Australia Post 4 State Customer Code* is a barcode used by
Australia Post to encode the data on letter mail.

Also known as: 4SCC, 4 State Customer Code.

Uses:

* Letter mail in Australia, carrying the Delivery Point Identifier
(DPID) for automated sorting.

Standards: Australia Post Customer Barcode Technical Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The first two digits of the data field are the mandatory Format
Control Code (FCC), either:
** `11`: Customer Barcode 1 ("Standard Customer Barcode")
** `45`: Reply Paid Barcode
** `59`: Customer Barcode 2
** `62`: Customer Barcode 3
** `87`: Routing Barcode
** `92`: Redirection Barcode
* The next eight characters are digits that specify the mandatory DPID.
* Any remaining characters specify the customer information field, which
FCCs `11`, `45`, `87` and `92` do not have. FCC `59` takes up to 8
digits or 5 characters, and FCC `62` up to 15 digits or 10 characters,
in one of two alphabets:
** The *custinfoenc* option should be supplied as `custinfoenc=numeric`
if the customer information field is to be encoded using the numeric
alphabet which can contain the digits 0-9.
** Otherwise the customer information field is encoded using the default
character encoding, `custinfoenc=character`, which permits any of the
following characters:
*** Upper case letters `A-Z`
*** Lower case letters `a-z`
*** Digits `0-9`
*** Symbols `space` and `++#++`

===== Examples

FCC 62 symbol with character customer data:

....
Data:    6279438541AaaB 155
Options: custinfoenc=character includetext
Encoder: auspost
....

==== Canada Post PostBar

*Canada Post PostBar* is the family of 4-state barcodes of Canada Post
that is disclosed in US Patent 5,602,382, each with a Data Content
Identifier (DCI) giving its structure and Reed-Solomon error correction
over GF(64).

Uses:

* Sortation and tracking of mail by Canada Post.

Standards: US Patent 5,602,382 - Mail piece bar code having a data
content identifier; Canada Post 4-State Bar Code Handbook (bar
dimensions).

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the DCI followed by the fields of the format, which
is selected by the length of the data:
** PostBar.C10 (11 characters, 56 bars), applied by Canada Post's
machines: a DCI from `V` to `Z`, the six-character postal code, and the
four bars of the machine ID as digits from `0` (full bar) to `3`
(tracker).
** PostBar.G12 (12 characters, 49 bars), for international mail: a DCI
from `1` to `9`, the three-digit country code, and an eight-character
postal code padded with spaces.
** PostBar.S21 (21 characters, 79 bars), for customer services: a DCI
from `M` to `U`, the bar code sequencer, `0` for a single symbol or `1`
or `2` for the first or second of two, and 19 characters of service
information.
** PostBar.D22 (22 characters, 79 bars), applied by customers to
domestic mail: a DCI from `A` to `L`, the six-character postal code, a
four-character address locator and eleven characters of customer
information.
* Postal codes are written without a space, alternating letters and
digits. The other fields contain spaces, upper case letters and digits.
* The structures of Canada Post's Postal Encoding Module, such as D52.01
and D82.02, are not available, since their encodation is not published.

===== Examples

A domestic bar code, PostBar.D22:

....
Data:    CH0H0H01420NOTEPAPER01
Options:
Encoder: postbar
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

An international bar code, PostBar.G12:

....
Data:    9826AB12 3CD
Options:
Encoder: postbar
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cg==]

==== CEPNet

The *CEPNet* barcode symbology is used by Correios, the Brazilian postal
service, to encode the CEP postal code on letter mail. It has the bars
of <<_usps_postnet,USPS POSTNET>>.

Uses:

* Brazilian mail.

Standards: Correios Guia Técnico - CEPNet e Código 2D para Triagem e
Endereçamento.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains the eight digits of the CEP, without a dash.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless
*validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the check digit appear in the
human readable text.
* The guide gives bars from 0.015 to 0.025 inches wide at 22 {plus}/- 2
bars per inch, with tall bars from 0.115 to 0.135 inches high. The
encoder's defaults are the midpoints, bars 0.020 inches wide and 0.125
inches high.

===== Examples

....
Data:    01234567
Options: includetext
Encoder: cepnet
....

==== DPD Parcel Label

The *DPD Parcel Label* barcode is a <<_code_128,Code 128>> barcode on
the parcel labels of the DPD (Geopost) parcel carriers that carries the
destination postal code, the tracking number, the service code and the
destination country.

Uses:

* Routing and tracking of parcels by the DPD group.

Standards: Geopost Barcode & Label Layout Specification (GeoLabel); DPD
Parcel Label Specification, whose section 6.1.2 describes the relabel.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the 27 characters that follow the identification
tag, optionally preceded by the tag. The tag is `%` unless it is given:
** The destination postal code, seven characters padded on the left with
zeros.
** The tracking number, a four-digit range code and a ten-digit parcel
number, the first two characters of which may be letters.
** The three-digit service code.
** The three-digit destination country or network code.
* The postal code and the first two characters of the tracking number
may be upper case letters or digits. The remaining characters are
digits.
* The human readable text is the data in groups, followed by its ISO/IEC
7064 MOD 37,36 check character, which is not encoded in the barcode.
* The *relabel* option creates the barcode of a relabel, which has no
identification tag and half the height.
* The default height is one inch, or half an inch for a relabel. The
X-dimension of the specification is from 0.375mm to 0.5mm, or to 0.4mm
for thermal printing, and the height 25mm, or 12.5mm for a relabel.

===== Examples

....
Data:    005432155550001234567101826
Options: includetext
Encoder: dpd
....

==== Deutsche Post Identcode

*Deutsche Post Identcode* is an implementation of the
<<_interleaved_2_of_5,Interleaved 2 of 5>> barcode symbology that is
used by Deutsche Post to identify parcels for tracking.

Also known as: DHL Identcode.

Uses:

* Deutsche Post (DHL) parcels: the parcel's identification for tracking.

Standards: Deutsche Post AG Identcode.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of a consecutive string of eleven or twelve digits
consisting of:
** Two-digit primary distribution centre identifier
** Three-digit customer identifier
** Six-digit mail piece identifier
** One-digit check digit (may be omitted)
* If eleven digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated
automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    563102430313
Options: includetext
Encoder: identcode
....

....
Data:    56310243031
Options: includetext
Encoder: identcode
....

==== Deutsche Post Leitcode

*Deutsche Post Leitcode* is an implementation of the
<<_interleaved_2_of_5,Interleaved 2 of 5>> barcode symbology that is
used by Deutsche Post for mail routing.

Also known as: DHL Leitcode.

Uses:

* Deutsche Post (DHL) parcels: the destination's routing code (postcode,
street and house number).

Standards: Deutsche Post AG Leitcode.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of a consecutive string of thirteen or fourteen
digits consisting of:
** Five-digit postal code
** Three-digit street identifier
** Three-digit house number
** Two-digit product code
** One-digit check digit (may be omitted)
* If thirteen digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated
automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    21348075016401
Options: includetext
Encoder: leitcode
....

....
Data:    2134807501640
Options: includetext
Encoder: leitcode
....

==== Japan Post 4 State Barcode

The *Japan Post 4 state barcode* symbology is used by the Japan Post
service to encode the delivery point identifier on letter mail.

Also known as: Kasutama Barcode, Customer Barcode.

Uses:

* Mail in Japan: the customer barcode, carrying the postcode and
address.

Standards: Japan Post Customer Barcode Technical Specification.

===== Data and Options

* The data may contain any of the following characters:
** Capital letters `A-Z`
** Digits `0-9`
** Hyphen `-`
* The data is at most 20 characters, each letter counting as two.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digit
appear in the human readable text.

===== Examples

A delivery point identifier:

....
Data:    6540123789-A-K-Z
Options:
Encoder: japanpost
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,]

==== Korea Post

The *Korea Post* customer barcode encodes a six-digit Korean postcode
and a check digit for the automatic sorting of letter mail. Each digit
is five equally spaced positions holding three bars, followed by a bar
that separates it from the next, and the digits are printed from the
least significant.

Korea Post replaced the six-digit postcodes with five-digit postcodes in
August 2015.

Uses:

* Korean bulk mail, printed by the sender.

Standards: Korea Post customer barcode, as described by ETRI
(Electronics and Telecommunications Trends, 1999).

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains the six digits of the postcode.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless
*validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the check digit appear in the
human readable text.

===== Examples

....
Data:    123456
Options: includetext
Encoder: koreapost
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMTg1IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjE4IiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTg1IDE4Ij4KPGRlZnM{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtMSI{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPC9zdmc{plus}Cg==]

==== MaxiCode

The *MaxiCode* barcode symbology is a 2D barcode based on a hexagonal
matrix surrounding a bulls eye pattern. It can encode a structured
carrier message and full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: UPS Code, Code 6, Dense Code.

Uses:

* UPS parcel labels, carrying the structured carrier message (postcode,
country and service class).

Variants:

* <<_ups_maxicode,UPS MaxiCode>> is a variant of MaxiCode that validates
the UPS message of a package label.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16023, ANSI/AIM BC10 - ISS MaxiCode.

===== Data and Options

* The *mode* option is used to specify how the data is structured in the
symbol:
** `mode=2` - Formatted data containing a Structured Carrier Message
with a numeric (US domestic) postal code.
** `mode=3` - Formatted data containing a Structured Carrier Message
with an alphanumeric (international) postal code.
** `mode=4` - Unstructured extended ASCII data using standard error
correction.
** `mode=5` - Unstructured extended ASCII data using enhanced error
correction.
** `mode=6` - Barcode reader programming.
* If *mode* is unspecified the encoder will default to selecting
`mode=5` if the encoded length of the input data permits enhanced error
correction, otherwise it will select `mode=4` which provides standard
error correction.
* The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with
ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other
code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
* If `mode=4`, `mode=5` or `mode=6` the data field may contain any
extended ASCII data.
* If `mode=2` or `mode=3` the data field must begin with a properly
structured carrier message, followed by any extended ASCII data.
* The structured carrier message contains a postal code, a three-digit
ISO country code and a three-digit class of service separated by _GS_
(ASCII 29) characters. It is formatted in the data field as follows:
`++[++postal code++]++^029++[++country code++]++^029++[++service class++]++^029`.
If `mode=2` the postcode is up to nine digits, whilst if `mode=3` the
postcode is up to six characters from capital letters, digits, space and
`"++#++$%&'()++*++{plus},-./:`.
* Alternatively, messages may begin with the special application field
identifier "++[++)++>{++RS}01++{++GS}yy" where "++{++RS}" represents
ASCII value 30, "++{++GS}" represents ASCII value 29 and "yy" is a
two-digit year. In *parse* mode this is represented as
`++[++)++>++^03001^029yy`. If `mode=2` or `mode=3` this must be
immediately followed by the structured carrier message.
* The *sam* option specifies this symbol to be part of multi-part
structured data held in up to eight symbols. For example `sam=25`
specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five symbols.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options are an alternative to *sam* that
give the position and the total separately, for example
`sampos=2 samtotal=5`. They cannot be combined with *sam*.

===== Rendering

* Dark hexagons are drawn 0.12mm narrower than the module pitch, as the
specification requires, and <<_inkspread,inkspread>> reduces them
further, so `inkspread=0` gives the nominal dimensions.
* MaxiCode is a fixed-size symbology so <<_strictspec,strictspec>>
bounds the X-dimension to the permitted symbol width of 24mm to 27mm.
* Bitmap output should use <<_gridfit,gridfit>>, which follows the
practical printing guidance of ISO/IEC 16023 Annex J: whole device
pixels per module and, at resolutions below about 850 DPI, pixel fonts
for the hexagons and finder pattern.

===== Examples

Identical symbols encoding unstructured data, the latter using the parse
option:

....
Data:    This is MaxiCode
Options:
Encoder: maxicode
....

....
Data:    This is Maxi^067ode
Options: parse
Encoder: maxicode
....

==== UPS MaxiCode

*UPS MaxiCode* is the use of <<_maxicode,MaxiCode>> on UPS package
labels, carrying a structured carrier message with the destination
postal code, country and class of service, followed by the UPS shipment
details.

Uses:

* UPS package labels.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16023 MaxiCode; UPS Guide to Bar Coding, which is
available to UPS customers.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the message of 14 fields separated by GS characters,
optionally enclosed by the header `++[++)++>{++RS}01++{++GS}yy`, where
yy is the two digit format version, and the trailer `++{++RS}++{++EOT}`:
** The ship to postal code, of five or nine digits, or up to six upper
case letters, digits or spaces.
** The three digit ship to country code.
** The three digit class of service.
** The tracking number, ten upper case letters or digits.
** The carrier code, `UPSN`.
** The shipper number, six upper case letters or digits.
** The three digit day of the year of pickup.
** The shipment ID, of up to 30 characters, which may be empty.
** The package of packages, as `n/x`.
** The weight in pounds, of up to three digits, which may be empty.
** The address validation flag, `Y` or `N`.
** The ship to address, of up to 35 characters, which may be empty.
** The ship to city, of up to 20 characters.
** The ship to state, two upper case letters.
* The symbol is in mode 2 for a postal code of five or nine digits,
otherwise in mode 3.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying GS as `^029`, RS as `^030` and EOT as `^004`.

===== Examples

....
Data:    [)>^030\
         01^02996\
         123450001^029\
         840^029\
         001^029\
         1Z12345678^029\
         UPSN^029\
         A1B2C3^029\
         042^029\
         8901234^029\
         1/2^029\
         5^029\
         Y^029\
         12 EXAMPLE ST^029\
         SPRINGTON^029\
         CA^030^004
Options: parse
Encoder: upsmaxicode
....

==== Royal Mail 4 State Customer Code

The *Royal Mail 4 State Customer Code* is a barcode symbology used by
Royal Mail to encode the postcode and delivery point identifier on
letter mail.

Also known as: RM4SCC, CBC, BPO 4 State Code.

Uses:

* UK business mail sorted by postcode and delivery point, now largely
replaced by <<_mailmark,Mailmark>>.

Standards: BS 14500.

===== Data and Options

* The data may contain any of the following characters from the postcode
and DPID:
** Capital letters A-Z
** Digits 0-9
* The mandatory check character is calculated automatically, unless
*validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character of the data to be
the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the check character appear in
the human readable text.

===== Examples

A postcode and delivery point identifier:

....
Data:    LE28HS9Z
Options: includetext
Encoder: royalmail
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMTQ0IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjIxIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTQ0IDIxIj4KPGRlZnM{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNiI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPC9nPgo8L2RlZnM{plus}{plus}]

==== Mailmark

*Royal Mail Mailmark* is an implementation of the
<<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> (ECC 200) barcode symbology for application
within the Royal Mail postal system.

Uses:

* UK mail sorted and tracked by Royal Mail.

Variants:

* <<_mailmark_4_state,Royal Mail Mailmark 4-state>> is the 4-state
barcode form of Mailmark, for mailers that cannot print Data Matrix.

Standards: Royal Mail Mailmark Barcode Definition Document.

===== Data and Options

* The data field input consists of 45 characters of Mailmark structured
data (including required space padding) followed by variable-length,
free-formatted customer data.
* Note: Due to the fixed-length field format of the message data it is
important to carefully preserve spaces in the data field.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The mandatory *type* option is used to specify the size of the symbol,
either `7` (24x24), `9` (32x32) or `29` (16x48).

===== Examples

A type 29 (16x48) symbol:

....
Data:    JGB 012100123412345678AB19XY1A 0             www.xyz.com
Options: type=29
Encoder: mailmark
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

==== Mailmark 4-state

*Royal Mail Mailmark 4-state* is a 4-state barcode for application
within the Royal Mail postal system, for mailers that cannot print the
<<_mailmark,Data Matrix>> form of Mailmark. It carries the mailing's
identifiers and destination postcode with Reed-Solomon error correction.

Uses:

* UK machine-readable Low Sort and Unsorted letters sorted and tracked
by Royal Mail.
* Manual Mailmark parcels and general large letters.

Standards: Royal Mail Mailmark Barcode Definition Document; Royal Mail
Mailmark barcode C and barcode L encoding and decoding instructions.

===== Data and Options

* The data field consists of the fixed-length Mailmark fields, including
any space padding: 22 characters for barcode C (66 bars) or 26
characters for barcode L (78 bars):
** Format, `0` to `4`.
** Version ID, `1`.
** Class, `0` to `9` or `A` to `E`.
** Supply Chain ID, two digits for barcode C or six for barcode L.
** Item ID, eight digits.
** Destination Post Code plus Delivery Point Suffix, nine characters: a
full postcode followed by its two-character Delivery Point Suffix,
padded with spaces at the end, or `XY11` followed by five spaces for an
international destination.
* Note: Due to the fixed-length field format of the data it is important
to carefully preserve spaces in the data field.

===== Examples

A barcode C:

....
Data:    1101234567890ZZ999ZZ1A
Options:
Encoder: mailmark4state
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A barcode L:

==== Royal TNT Post 4 state barcode

The *Royal TNT Post 4 state barcode* symbology is used by PostNL to
encode the delivery point identifier on letter mail.

Also known as: KIX, Klant IndeX.

Uses:

* Mail in the Netherlands (PostNL), carrying the postcode and house
number.

Standards: TPG Post Kix Code Specification.

===== Data and Options

* The data may contain:
** Capital letters `A-Z`
** Digits `0-9`

===== Examples

A delivery point identifier:

....
Data:    1231FZ13XHS
Options: includetext
Encoder: kix
....

==== UPU S10

*UPU S10* is a <<_code_128,Code 128>> barcode carrying the 13-character
S10 identifier of the Universal Postal Union, which identifies postal
items, such as registered mail and parcels, as they pass between postal
operators.

Uses:

* International tracked postal items.
* Domestic postal items of many postal operators.

Standards: UPU S10 - Identification of postal items - 13-character
identifier.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the S10 identifier: a two-letter service indicator,
an eight-digit serial number, a check digit and the two-letter ISO
country code of the issuing postal operator, without spaces.
* If the check digit is omitted then the encoder will calculate and add
it. If it is given then it is verified.
* Service indicators beginning with J, K, S, T or W are reserved and are
refused.
* The human readable text is spaced in groups for readability.
* The default height is half an inch. The X-dimension of the standard is
from 0.25mm to 0.51mm, with a minimum of 0.33mm recommended. The height
is at least 9mm and 15% of the width of the symbol, with a minimum of
12.5mm recommended.

===== Examples

....
Data:    EE471108151FR
Options: includetext
Encoder: upus10
....

==== USPS Intelligent Mail

The *USPS Intelligent Mail* barcode is used by the US Postal Service to
encode the delivery and sender information on letter mail.

Also known as: USPS OneCode.

Uses:

* US letters and flats, for automation prices and tracking.

Standards: USPS-B-3200.

===== Data and Options

* The data contains 20, 25, 29 or 31 digits representing the following:
** Barcode Identifier - two digits
** Service Type Identifier - three digits
** Mailer ID, Sequence Number - either six then nine digits respectively
or nine then six digits respectively
** Delivery Point ZIP Code - none, five, nine or eleven digits
* An 11-bit CRC is added automatically.

===== Examples

A 31-digit mail tracking barcode:

....
Data:    0123456709498765432101234567891
Options: includetext
Encoder: onecode
....

==== USPS POSTNET

The *USPS POSTNET* barcode symbology is used by the US Postal Service to
encode the ZIP code information on letter mail.

Uses:

* US mail, superseded by the
<<_usps_intelligent_mail,USPS Intelligent Mail>> barcode.

Variants:

* <<_cepnet,CEPNet>> has the bars of POSTNET and carries the Brazilian
CEP postal code.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains five, nine or eleven digits (ZIP, ZIP{plus}4,
or ZIP{plus}4 and delivery point), without dashes.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless
*validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the check digit appear in the
human readable text.

===== Examples

A ZIP{plus}4{plus}delivery point code:

....
Data:    12345123412
Options:
Encoder: postnet
....

==== USPS PLANET

The *USPS PLANET* barcode symbology is used by the US Postal Service to
track letter mail.

Uses:

* US mail, superseded by the
<<_usps_intelligent_mail,USPS Intelligent Mail>> barcode.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains eleven or thirteen digits, without dashes.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless
*validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the check digit appear in the
human readable text.

===== Examples

An 11-digit PLANET code:

....
Data:    01234567890
Options:
Encoder: planet
....

==== USPS FIM Symbols

The *symbol* encoder generates the USPS Facing Identification Marks.

Uses:

* Facing identification marks on US business reply and courtesy reply
mail.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

===== Data and Options

* The data field accepts one of the following values:
** `fima` - FIM-A
** `fimb` - FIM-B
** `fimc` - FIM-C
** `fimd` - FIM-D
** `fime` - FIM-E

===== Examples

A USPS FIM A symbol:

....
Data:    fima
Options: 
Encoder: symbol
....

=== Pharmaceutical Symbols

==== Italian Pharmacode

*Italian Pharmacode* is an implementation of the <<_code_39,Code 39>>
barcode symbology that is used for pharmaceutical products in Italy.

Also known as: Code 32, IMH, Radix 32.

Uses:

* Medicines in Italy: the Codice Farmaceutico (AIC) on packs.

Standards: Italian Ministerial Decree 2003.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must contain either eight or nine digits from the code.
The leading _A_ which is provided in some applications must be omitted;
it is added to the human readable text.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically if it is not
provided, otherwise the provided check digit is verified.

===== Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    012345676
Options: includetext
Encoder: code32
....

....
Data:    01234567
Options: includetext
Encoder: code32
....

==== Pharmacode

*Pharmacode* is a binary barcode symbology that is used by the
pharmaceutical industry.

Also known as: Pharmaceutical Binary Code, Laetus Code.

Uses:

* Checking the printed packaging materials of pharmaceuticals on
packaging lines, rather than identifying an item in trade.

Variants:

* <<_two_track_pharmacode,Two-track Pharmacode>> is a variant of the
Pharmacode barcode.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must contain a number between `3` and `131070`
inclusive.
* The *nwidth*, *wwidth* and *swidth* options can be used to specify a
custom width, in modules, for the narrow bars, wide bars and inter-bar
spaces respectively. The defaults are 1, 3 and 2.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    117480
Options:
Encoder: pharmacode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODQiIGhlaWdodD0iNzIiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4NCA3MiI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A symbol with custom bar widths:

....
Data:    117480
Options: nwidth=2 wwidth=6 swidth=4
Encoder: pharmacode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Two-Track Pharmacode

*Two-Track Pharmacode* is a binary barcode symbology used by the
pharmaceutical industry.

Also known as: Two-track Pharmaceutical Binary Code, Two-track Laetus
Code.

Uses:

* Checking the printed packaging materials of pharmaceuticals on
packaging lines, rather than identifying an item in trade.

Variants:

* <<_pharmacode,Pharmacode>> is the one-track form.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must contain a number between `4` and `64570080`
inclusive.
* The *height* option specifies the height of each of the two tracks in
inches, so a full-height bar is twice as tall. The default is 4mm
(`height=0.1575`).

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    117480
Options:
Encoder: pharmacode2
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODAiIGhlaWdodD0iMjMiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4MCAyMyI{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== PZN

*PZN* is a discrete, fixed length, self-checking barcode symbology used
for pharmaceutical products in Germany.

Also known as: Pharmazentralnummer.

Uses:

* Medicines in Germany: the Pharmazentralnummer (PZN) on packs.

Variants:

* PZN7 is the seven-digit format.
* PZN8 is the eight-digit format.

Standards: IFA Coding System PZN.

===== Data and Options

* For the default PZN7 encoding, the data field must contain six digits
or seven digits.
* The *pzn8* option specifies that a PZN8 symbol is required, in which
case the data field must contain seven digits or eight digits.
* The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically if not provided,
otherwise the provided check digit is verified.
* A number whose check value is 10 has no valid check digit and cannot
be encoded.

===== Examples

Identical PZN7 symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

....
Data:    1234562
Options: includetext
Encoder: pzn
....

....
Data:    123456
Options: includetext
Encoder: pzn
....
