==== PPN-Code

The *PPN-Code* is a <<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> symbol on the packs of
pharmaceutical products that carries the Pharmacy Product Number (PPN),
with the serial number, batch number and expiry date used to verify the
pack, as data elements with ASC MH10 Data Identifiers in the ISO/IEC
15434 Format 06 envelope.

Uses:

* Packs of pharmaceutical products in Germany and other markets whose
numbering agencies have a PRA Code, including verification under the EU
Falsified Medicines Directive (securPharm).

Standards: IFA PPN-Code Specification for Retail Packaging; ISO/IEC
15434; ISO/IEC 15418; ISO/IEC 16022.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains the data elements, each a Data Identifier
followed by its data, separated by GS characters. The envelope is added
by the encoder.
* The elements are in any order, and those of the specification are
validated:
** `9N` - The Pharmacy Product Number, which is required: a PRA Code,
the product number and two check digits. For PRA Code `11` the product
number is a German PZN, whose check digit is also verified.
** `S` - The serial number, up to 20 characters of the GS1 character set
82.
** `1T` - The batch number, up to 20 characters of the GS1 character set
82.
** `D` - The expiry date, as YYMMDD, with day `00` for the month alone.
** `8P` - An additional GTIN or NTIN, which may be repeated.
* Other Data Identifiers may be included.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying the GS separators as `^029`.
* The options of <<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>> are available, such as
*format=rectangle* or *dmre* for a rectangular symbol.
* The X-dimension of the specification is from 0.25mm to 0.99mm,
typically 0.35mm.

===== Examples

....
Data:    9N112048163909^029\
         1TBATCH42^029\
         D281200^029\
         SA1B2C3D4E5
Options: parse
Encoder: ppncode
....

=== HIBC Symbols

*HIBC barcodes* use a number of general symbologies as carrier symbols
for data structured according to the LIC and PAS structured data
definitions.

Uses:

* Healthcare products and medical devices labelled to the Health
Industry Bar Code (HIBC) standards, including the UDI of devices issued
through HIBCC.

Variants:

* <<_hibc_code_39,HIBC Code 39>> is a variant of <<_code_39,Code 39>>.
* <<_hibc_code_128,HIBC Code 128>> is a variant of
<<_code_128,Code 128>>.
* <<_hibc_pdf417,HIBC PDF417>> is a variant of <<_pdf417,PDF417>>.
* <<_hibc_micropdf417,HIBC MicroPDF417>> is a variant of
<<_micropdf417,MicroPDF417>>.
* <<_hibc_qr_code,HIBC QR Code>> is a variant of <<_qr_code,QR Code>>.
* <<_hibc_data_matrix,HIBC Data Matrix>> is a variant of
<<_data_matrix,Data Matrix>>.
* <<_hibc_data_matrix_rectangular,HIBC Data Matrix Rectangular>> is a
variant of <<_data_matrix_rectangular,Data Matrix Rectangular>>.
* <<_hibc_codablock_f,HIBC Codablock F>> is a variant of
<<_codablock_f,Codablock F>>.
* <<_hibc_aztec_code,HIBC Aztec Code>> is a variant of
<<_aztec_code,Aztec Code>>.

Data syntax: HIBC LIC/PAS.

Standards: ANSI/HIBC Provider Applications Standard, ANSI/HIBC Supplier
Labelling Standard, ANSI/HIBC Positive Identification for Patient
Safety, ANSI/HIBC Syntax Standard.

===== Data and Options

* The data is the HIBC LIC or PAS data, without the leading _{plus}_,
and contains only digits, capital letters, space and `-.$/{plus}%`.
* The HIBC _{plus}_ character is prefixed automatically.
* The mandatory HIBC check character is automatically appended to the
input, unless *validatecheck* is given.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character of the data to be
the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.

==== HIBC Code 39

....
Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options: includetext

=== Less-used Symbols

==== BC412

The *BC412* barcode symbology is a single-width, variable-length barcode
that is used for silicon wafer identification by the semiconductor
manufacturing industry.

Also known as: BC412 SEMI, BC412 IBM.

Uses:

* Silicon wafer identification in semiconductor fabs (SEMI T1).

Standards: SEMI T1.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can hold any of the following:
** Numbers 0-9
** Capital letters A-Z, excluding O
* The *includestartstop* option adds start and stop bars.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check character.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character of the data (the
second with *semi*) to be the check character and refuses the data if it
is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check character
appear in the human readable text.
* The *semi* option enables conformance to the SEMI standard by enabling
start and stop bars and a check character, which is placed in the second
position rather than appended. The data must be 7 to 18 characters.
* The *inkspread* option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.

===== Examples

A symbol with a check character:

....
Data:    BC412
Options: includecheck
Encoder: bc412
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODkiIGhlaWdodD0iNzIiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4OSA3MiI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A symbol with start and stop bars:

....
Data:    BC412
Options: includestartstop
Encoder: bc412
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODYiIGhlaWdodD0iNzIiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4NiA3MiI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

A SEMI-compliant symbol:

....
Data:    BC412SEMIEXAMPLE
Options: semi
Encoder: bc412
....

==== Channel Code

*Channel Code* is a linear, continuous, self-checking, bidirectional
barcode symbology that encodes between two and seven digits in a short
space.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC12 - USS Channel Code.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can hold zero prefixed values from any of the following
ranges:
** Channel 3: `00-26`
** Channel 4: `000-292`
** Channel 5: `0000-3493`
** Channel 6: `00000-44072`
** Channel 7: `000000-576688`
** Channel 8: `0000000-7742862`
* The channel is determined to be one more than the number of digits
given in the data field.
* The *shortfinder* option generates a symbol with a shortened finder
pattern.
* The *includecheck* option appends an optional check bar suffix.

===== Examples

A channel 3 symbol holding the value five:

....
Data:    05
Options: includetext
Encoder: channelcode
....

==== Codabar

*Codabar* is a linear, discrete, self-checking, bidirectional barcode
symbology that can encode digits, six symbols and four delimiter
characters.

Also known as: Rationalized Codabar, Ames Code, NW-7, USD-4,
USS-Codabar, ABC Codabar, Monarch, Code 2 of 7.

Uses:

* Library books and library cards.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC3 - USS Codabar, BS EN 798.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must start and stop with one of the following
delimiters
** `ABCD`
** `TNE++*++` (with the _altstartstop_ option)
* The data field can otherwise hold any of the following
** Digits 0-9
** Symbols `-$:/.{plus}`
* The *altstartstop* option specifies that the alternative set of
delimiter characters is in use.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check character.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last character before the stop
delimiter to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check character
appear in the human readable text.

===== Examples

A symbol with a check digit:

....
Data:    A0123456789B
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: rationalizedCodabar
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMTc5IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTc5IDgwIj4KPGRlZnM{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNCI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNSI{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNyI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtOCI{plus}{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPC9nPgo8L2RlZnM{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A symbol with alternative start/stop delimiters:

....
Data:    T0123456789N
Options: altstartstop includetext
Encoder: rationalizedCodabar
....

==== Codablock F

The *Codablock F* barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that
consists of a number of stacked <<_code_128,Code 128>> symbols. It can
encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Variants:

* <<_hibc_symbols,HIBC Codablock F>> is a variant of Codablock F that
should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
* <<_codablock_a,Codablock A>> is the related symbology whose rows are
Code 39 symbols.

Standards: USS Codablock F.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any extended-ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* _FNC4_ function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the
encoding of extended ASCII characters.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
* The *columns* option specifies the number of columns in the symbol,
from 4 to 62, default 8.
* The *rows* option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between
2 and 44.
* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest
number of rows that can hold the given data.
* The *rowheight* option specifies the height of the bars in each row in
modules, from 8 to 50. The default is 10.
* The *sepheight* option specifies the height of the separator bars
enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    Codablock F
Options:
Encoder: codablockf
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,]

A symbol with fixed dimensions:

....
Data:    CODABLOCK F 34567890123456789010040digit
Options: columns=8 rows=5
Encoder: codablockf
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cg==]

A symbol with custom row and separator heights:

....
Data:    Tall bars, fat separators
Options: columns=10 rows=8 rowheight=12 sepheight=2
Encoder: codablockf
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Codablock A

The *Codablock A* barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that
consists of a number of stacked <<_code_39,Code 39>> symbols, each row a
complete Code 39 symbol. It encodes the Code 39 character set.

Also known as: Codablock 39, Codablock Alpha.

Standards: AIM HD/13-005 Historical Document - Codablock A (ICS
Codablock A symbology specification).

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain upper case letters, digits and the
characters `-`, `.`, space, `$`, `/`, `{plus}` and `%`, up to 1340
characters.
* Each row begins and ends with a row indicator, the first row's giving
the number of rows and the others the position of the row. A symbol of a
single row has only the indicator at its start. Two check characters
calculated over all of the data end the last row, preceded by filler
spaces when the data does not fill it.
* The *columns* option specifies the number of data characters in each
row, from 1 to 61. The default is 8.
* The *rows* option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, from 1
to 22.
* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest
number of rows that can hold the given data.
* The *rowheight* option specifies the height of the bars in each row in
modules, at least 8. The default is the minimum height in the
specification for the number of columns, which is about a twentieth of
the width of a row and at least 8.
* The *sepheight* option specifies the height of the separator bars
enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

===== Examples

....
Data:    THE QUICK BROWN FOX JUMPS OVER THE LAZY DOG
Options: columns=10
Encoder: codablocka
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Code 11

*Code 11* is a linear, discrete, non-self-checking, bidirectional,
numeric barcode symbology that is primarily used for labelling
telecommunication equipment.

Also known as: USD-8.

Uses:

* Labelling telecommunications equipment.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of digits and the dash character _-_.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digits.
* For fewer than 10 data characters a single check digit is used.
* For 10 or more data characters two check digits are used.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data (the last
two digits when the data is twelve or more characters long) to be the
check digits and refuses the data if they are wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digits
appear in the human readable text.

===== Examples

A symbol with check digits:

....
Data:    0123456789
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: code11
....

==== Code 16K

The *Code 16K* barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that can
encode full 256 character extended-ASCII with the use of the _FNC4_
shift character.

Also known as: USS-16K.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC7 - USS Code 16K, BS EN 12323.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* _FNC4_ function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the
encoding of extended ASCII characters.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC2`: FNC2
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>. It is not
available with Structured Append.
* The *sam* option specifies this symbol to be part of multi-part
structured data held in up to nine symbols. For example `sam=25`
specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five symbols.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options are an alternative to *sam* that
give the position and the total separately, for example
`sampos=2 samtotal=5`. They cannot be combined with *sam*.
* The *rows* option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between
two and sixteen.
* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest
number of rows that can hold the given data.
* The *raw* option denotes that the data field is providing the input as
pre-encoded codewords in `^NNN` format, suitable for direct low-level
encoding.
* The *rowheight* option specifies the height of the bars in each row in
modules, from 8 to 50. The default is 8.
* The *sepheight* option specifies the height of the separator bars
enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    Abcd-1234567890-wxyZ
Options:
Encoder: code16k
....

==== Code 25

*Code 25* is a simple low density numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: Code 25, Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.

Variants:

* <<_iata_2_of_5,IATA 2 of 5>>, Computer Identics 2 of 5.
* <<_datalogic_2_of_5,Datalogic 2 of 5>>.
* <<_matrix_2_of_5,Matrix 2 of 5>>.
* <<_coop_2_of_5,COOP 2 of 5>>.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of any number of digits.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digit
appear in the human readable text.
* _Deprecated:_ The *version* option determines which variant to use:
** `version=industrial` (default) - Industrial 2 of 5.
** `version=iata` - _Deprecated: Consider <<_iata_2_of_5,IATA 2 of 5>>_
** `version=datalogic` - _Deprecated: Consider
<<_datalogic_2_of_5,Datalogic 2 of 5>>_
** `version=matrix` - _Deprecated: Consider
<<_matrix_2_of_5,Matrix 2 of 5>>_
** `version=coop` - _Deprecated: Consider <<_coop_2_of_5,COOP 2 of 5>>_

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    01234567
Options:
Encoder: code2of5
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

Industrial 2 of 5 with a check digit, using the dedicated encoder:

....
Data:    01234567
Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext
Encoder: industrial2of5
....

==== DotCode

The *DotCode* symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode that can encode
full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Ribbon Code.

Uses:

* High-speed marking on production lines, such as by inkjet.
* Unit packets of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU)
2018/574.

Variants:

* <<_gs1_dotcode,GS1 DotCode>> is a variant of DotCode that should be
used when encoding data that is in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.

Standards: AIM - ISS DotCode.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be
encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is
useful for specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1. _Recommendation: Consider <<_gs1_dotcode,GS1 DotCode>>
for encoding GS1 AI syntax data._
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data or of a
message segment that follows FNC3, e.g. `^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *ratio* option sets the width-to-height ratio of the symbol. The
default is 1.5.
* The *columns* and *rows* options are used to specify the size of the
symbol, each from 5 to 200, with an odd sum. When these are not
specified a symbol is generated that maintains the selected aspect
ratio.
* The *mask* option selects mask `0` to `3` instead of the best one.
* _Deprecated._ The *fast* option is used to enable the optional
high-speed symbol masking algorithm.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 35 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** The position and total are encoded at the end of the data, followed
by FNC2.
** Structured Append is not available with FNC3, for reader
initialisation or symbol separation, nor for GS1 DotCode symbols.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    This is DotCode
Options: inkspread=0.16
Encoder: dotcode
....

==== Ultracode

The *Ultracode* symbology is a colour, 2D matrix-style barcode symbology
that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Standards: AIM ISS - Ultracode.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level:
** `eclevel=EC1` - Low
** `eclevel=EC2` - Medium (default)
** `eclevel=EC3`
** `eclevel=EC4`
** `eclevel=EC5` - Highest
* _Deprecated_: `eclevel=EC0`, error detection only, is accepted only
with *rev=1*, the legacy revision.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append Group of 2 to 8 symbols, which a reader reassembles
into a single message. Both are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the group, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the group.
** The optional File Number of a Structured Append Group is not
supported.
** Structured Append is not available for revision 1 symbols, with FNC1
in first position, with FNC3 or with the *raw* option.

===== Examples

A symbol with increased error correction:

....
Data:    Nice colours!
Options: eclevel=EC3
Encoder: ultracode
....

==== IATA 2 of 5

*IATA 2 of 5* is a variant of the <<_code_25,Code 2 of 5>> barcode
symbology.

Also known as: Computer Identics 2 of 5.

Variants:

* <<_code_25,Industrial 2 of 5>>, Standard 2 of 5.
* <<_datalogic_2_of_5,Datalogic 2 of 5>>.
* <<_matrix_2_of_5,Matrix 2 of 5>>.
* <<_coop_2_of_5,COOP 2 of 5>>.

===== Data and Options

* The data consists of any number of digits.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digit of the data to be the
check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check digit
appear in the human readable text.

===== Examples

A symbol with a check digit:

....

Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext

....

==== Code 49

The *Code 49* barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that can
encode 128 character ASCII.

Also known as: USS-49.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC6 - USS Code 49.

===== Data and Options

* The input can consist of any ASCII data.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC2`: FNC2
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator at the start of the data, e.g. `^FNC@T...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>. Code 49 can encode
an upper case letter, or a lower case letter except with *append*, but
not two digits. It is not available with Structured Append.
* The *sam* option specifies this symbol is part of multi-part
structured data held in up to nine "mode 3" symbols. For example
`sam=25` specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five
symbols.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options are an alternative to *sam* that
give the position and the total separately, for example
`sampos=2 samtotal=5`. They cannot be combined with *sam*.
* The *append* option specifies that this symbol is an alphanumeric
continuation symbol ("mode 1").
* The *rows* option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between
_2_ and _8_.
* If *rows* is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest
number of rows that can hold the given data.
* The *rowheight* option specifies the height of the bars in each row in
modules, from _8_ to _50_. The default is _8_.
* The *sepheight* option specifies the height of the separator bars
enclosing the rows in modules, from _1_ to _5_. The default is _1_.

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    MULTIPLE ROWS IN CODE 49
Options:
Encoder: code49
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODEiIGhlaWdodD0iNDYiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4MSA0NiI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii04LjEiIHk9Ii00LjYiIHdpZHRoPSI5Ny4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjU1LjIiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii04LjEiIHk9Ii00LjYiIHdpZHRoPSI5Ny4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjU1LjIiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

....

Options: rows=8
Encoder: code49
....

==== Code One

*Code One* was the earliest public domain 2D matrix-style barcode. It
can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Code 1, Code 1S.

Standards: AIM USS - Code One.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data for _standard_
and _T-type_ symbols. The default interpretation of data by readers is
in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver,
characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel
Interpretation (ECI).
* Note: _S-type_ symbols are special in that they represent a numeric
value so may only contain digits.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters, e.g. `^029` for _GS_, etc.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI999999`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size and type of the
symbol:
** `version=A` to `version=H` - for standard format symbols (default
automatic selection)
** `version=T-16`, `version=T-32`, `version=T-48` - _T-type_ symbols
** `version=S-10`, `version=S-20`, `version=S-30` - _S-type_ symbols
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 128 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence. Up to 15 symbols
are encoded in Group mode, and more in Extended Group mode.
** Structured Append is not available for S-Type symbols, with FNC1 in
first or second position or with reader programming (FNC3).

===== Examples

A standard symbol, automatically sized:

....
Data:    Code One
Options:
Encoder: codeone
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMzYiIGhlaWdodD0iMzIiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAzNiAzMiI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii0zLjYiIHk9Ii0zLjIiIHdpZHRoPSI0My4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjM4LjQiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii0zLjYiIHk9Ii0zLjIiIHdpZHRoPSI0My4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjM4LjQiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A version C standard symbol:

....
Data:    Code One
Options: version=C
Encoder: codeone
....

==== Grid Matrix

The *Grid Matrix* symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that
can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII, with a compact encodation
of Chinese characters.

Standards: AIM ISS - Grid Matrix (AIMD014), GB/T 27766.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with GB 2312, in its
EUC-CN form that includes ASCII. When supported by the receiver
characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel
Interpretation (ECI), for example `^ECI000003` for ISO/IEC 8859-1.
* Data containing the two-byte EUC-CN form of GB 2312 characters is
encoded compactly.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^ECI000000` to `^ECI811799`: ECI indicators
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>.
** An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1
mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode
an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
** ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
* The *eclevel* option is used to specify the error correction level,
which reserves a proportion of the codewords for error correction:
** `eclevel=1` - 10%
** `eclevel=2` - 20%
** `eclevel=3` - 30%
** `eclevel=4` - 40%
** `eclevel=5` - 50%
** `eclevel=loose` - the minimum recommended level of the size of
symbol: 4 for version 1, 2 for version 2 and 1 for larger symbols. This
gives the greatest capacity.
** If unspecified the level is the recommended level of the size of
symbol: 5 for version 1, 4 for versions 2 and 3, and 3 for larger
symbols.
** Level 1 is not available in version 1 symbols.
* The *fixedeclevel* option will prevent the error correction level from
being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix
is possible.
* The *version* option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to
13, which is 18x18 to 162x162 modules.
* If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that
is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error
correction level.
* The *readerinit* option denotes that the symbol is used for
programming the barcode reader. It is not available with FNC1 in first
or second position.
* The *sampos* and *samtotal* options make the symbol one of a
Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader
reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
** *sampos* is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to
*samtotal*.
** *samtotal* is the number of symbols in the sequence.
** *samid* is a file signature from 0 to 255, the same in every symbol
of the sequence, which keeps the symbols of different sequences apart.
The default is 0.
** FNC1 in first or second position, and *readerinit*, are only
available in the first symbol of a sequence.

===== Examples

A symbol with the default error correction level:

....
Data:    Real knowledge is to know the extent of one's ignorance.
Options:
Encoder: gridmatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

The Chinese characters for "Welcome", given as their GB 2312 bytes:

....
Data:    ^187^182^211^173^185^226^193^217
Options: parse
Encoder: gridmatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODQiIGhlaWdodD0iODQiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4NCA4NCI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

UTF-8 text declared by ECI 26, with maximum error correction:

....
Data:    ^ECI000026Cr^195^168me br^195^187l^195^169e
Options: parse parsefnc eclevel=5
Encoder: gridmatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iODQiIGhlaWdodD0iODQiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA4NCA4NCI{plus}{plus}Cg==]

The first of a Structured Append sequence of two symbols that together
carry the opening of Moby-Dick:

....
Data:    Call me Ishmael. Some years ago - never mind how long precisely -
Options: sampos=1 samtotal=2 samid=42
Encoder: gridmatrix
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

==== Datastrip 2D

The *Datastrip 2D* symbology is a 2D barcode symbology in the form of a
strip of rows of a fixed width, read by a swipe reader, that carries a
field of text or binary data in compressed form with Reed-Solomon error
correction.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC15 - Datastrip 2D.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the content of a single field of the symbol, which
is text unless the *fieldtype* option says otherwise. It is compressed
in the zlib format before being encoded.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The *fieldtype* option gives the type of the field: `text` (the
default), `jpeg`, `binary` or `jpeg2000`, or a number from 0 to 255 for
a reserved or proprietary type, e.g. `fieldtype=16++#++21`.
* The *fieldsubtype* option gives the subtype of the field, from 0 to
255. The default is 0. For a text field 0 denotes US-ASCII, 2 UTF-16LE
and 3 UTF-16BE.
* The *disposition* option gives the disposition byte of the field, from
0 to 255. The default is 0. Bit 0 asks the reader not to display the
field and bit 1 asks it not to transmit the field; the other bits select
special processing of the field.
* The *stripid* option identifies the system that created the symbol, as
12 hexadecimal digits. The default is all zeros.
* The *columns* option is used to specify the width of the data area in
bytes, from 4 to 19. The default is 10. The symbol is eight modules per
column plus twelve modules of framing wide, within a quiet zone of two
modules at each side.
* The *rows* option is used to specify the number of data rows, from 31
to 3968. The symbol has four further rows of framing at each end. If
unspecified the encoder will select the fewest rows that hold the data
with at least a quarter of each block of bytes as error correction,
which tolerates the substitution of an eighth of the block, the minimum
that the specification requires.

===== Examples

A strip with the default width:

....
Data:    This is Datastrip 2D
Options:
Encoder: datastrip
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iOTYiIGhlaWdodD0iMzkiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA5NiAzOSI{plus}]

A narrow strip:

....
Data:    Marley was dead: to begin with. There is no doubt whatever about that. The register of his burial was signed by the clergyman, the clerk, the undertaker, and the chief mourner.
Options: columns=5
Encoder: datastrip
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNTYiIGhlaWdodD0iNTMiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA1NiA1MyI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjYiIHk9Ii01LjMiIHdpZHRoPSI2Ny4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjYzLjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjYiIHk9Ii01LjMiIHdpZHRoPSI2Ny4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjYzLjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A field of binary data:

....
Data:    ^000^001^002^253^254^255
Options: parse fieldtype=binary
Encoder: datastrip
....

==== MSI Plessey

*MSI Plessey* is a continuous, non-self-checking, arbitrary length,
numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: MSI, MSI Modified Plessey.

Uses:

* Shelf edge labels in retail stores.

Variants:

* <<_plessey,Plessey (UK)>> is the original barcode upon which MSI
Modified Plessey was based.

===== Data and Options

* The data can consist of any number of digits.
* The *includecheck* option calculates the check digit or check digits.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check characters
appear in the human readable text.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last digits of the data to be the
check digits of the *checktype*, as many as it adds, and refuses the
data if they are wrong.
* The *checktype* option is used with *includecheck* or *validatecheck*
to specify the type of checksum, either:
** `checktype=mod10` (default)
** `checktype=mod1010`
** `checktype=mod11`
** `checktype=ncrmod11`
** `checktype=mod1110`
** `checktype=ncrmod1110`
* The *badmod11* option allows a mod-11 checksum value of 10 to be
encoded with a pair of check digits _10_, with any *checktype*
containing mod11. Normally any input whose checksum evaluates to _10_ is
considered invalid having no correct representation.

===== Examples

A symbol with a mod-10 check digit:

....
Data:    0123456789
Options: includecheck includetext
Encoder: msi
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iMTU5IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTU5IDgwIj4KPGRlZnM{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtMyI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNCI{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNiI{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPGcgaWQ9ImdseXBoLTAtNyI{plus}{plus}{plus}CjwvZz4KPC9nPgo8L2RlZnM{plus}]

A symbol with mod-11 then mod-10 check digits:

....

Options: includecheck checktype=mod1110 includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: msi
....

Options: includecheck checktype=mod11 badmod11 includetext includecheckintext

....

[[marks--spencer]]
==== Marks & Spencer

*Marks & Spencer* is a barcode symbology derived from <<_ean_8,EAN-8>>
that is used by the UK retailer Marks & Spencer for internal purposes.
It differs from EAN-8 by having the centre guard bars removed and by
displaying an "M" and "S" on either side of the human readable text.

Also known as: M&S Barcode.

===== Data and Options

* The data field takes either seven or eight digits.
* Seven digits are taken as the eight-digit code without its leading
zero.
* The last digit is the check digit, which is verified.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.

===== Examples

A symbol with human-readable text:

....
Data:    06421182
Options: includetext
Encoder: mands
....

==== Plessey

*Plessey* is a continuous, arbitrary length barcode symbology for
encoding hexadecimal data.

Variants:

* <<_msi_plessey,MSI Modified Plessey>> is a variant of the Plessey (UK)
barcode developed by the MSI Data Corporation.
* <<_anker_code,Anker Code>> is a variant of the Plessey barcode used by
Anker point of sale systems.

===== Data and Options

* The data can contain any of the following:
** Digits `0-9`
** Capital letters `A-F`
* Two mandatory check characters implementing a CRC check are
automatically included.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last two characters of the data
to be the check characters and refuses the data if they are wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check characters
appear in the human readable text.
* The *unidirectional* option generates a unidirectional Plessey symbol.

===== Examples

Equivalent symbols, the latter displaying the two mandatory check
characters:

....
Data:    01234ABCD
Options: includetext
Encoder: plessey
....

==== Anker Code

*Anker Code* is a variant of the <<_plessey,Plessey>> barcode symbology
that was used on the labels of Anker point of sale systems before the
advent of EAN.

Standards: AIM HD/13-007 Historical Document - Anker, Plessey and MSI.

===== Data and Options

* The data can contain up to 28 of the following:
** Digits `0-9`
** Capital letters `A-F`
* Two mandatory check characters are automatically included. They are
the complement of the CRC check characters of Plessey.
* The symbol has the start pattern of Plessey and ends with a wide
termination bar and the reverse code, which allows reading in either
direction.
* The *validatecheck* option takes the last two characters of the data
to be the check characters and refuses the data if they are wrong.
* The *includecheckintext* option makes the calculated check characters
appear in the human readable text.

===== Examples

....
Data:    1234567890
Options: includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: anker
....

==== PosiCode

*PosiCode* is a continuous, variable length, non-self-checking,
bidirectional barcode symbology that is designed for use within printing
processes where it is difficult to precisely control the width of a bar.

Uses:

* Direct part marking where bar widths are hard to control, such as
laser engraving, chemical etching, dot peen or indent marking.

Standards: ITS PosiCode.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can hold the following:
** For _standard_ symbols: Any extended ASCII data. The default
interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
*** _FNC4_ function characters will be inserted automatically to allow
the encoding of extended ASCII characters.
** For _limited_ symbols: letters `A-Z`, digits `0-9`, symbols `-` and
`.`
* The *version* option is used to specify the variant of the symbol,
either:
** `version=a` (default)
** `version=b`
** `version=limiteda`
** `version=limitedb`
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters, e.g. `^029` for _GS_, etc.
* When the *parsefnc* option is specified, non-data function characters
can be specified by escape sequences:
** `^FNC1`: FNC1
** `^FNC2`: FNC2
** `^FNC3`: FNC3
** `^FNC@`: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application
indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g.
`^FNC@T...` or `^FNC@99...`. See
<<_fnc1_in_second_position,FNC1 in second position>>. It is not
available in the limited versions.
* The *inkspread* option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.

===== Examples

====== PosiCode

Equivalent ways to generate a PosiCode A symbol:

....
Data:    Abc123
Options: 
Encoder: posicode
....

....
Data:    Abc123
Options: version=a
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

PosiCode A including a _GS_ (ASCII 29) character:

....
Data:    AB^029CD
Options: parse
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

PosiCode A including an _FNC2_ special character:

....
Data:    AB^FNC2CD
Options: parsefnc
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

PosiCode B symbol with widened bars:

....
Data:    Abc123
Options: version=b inkspread=-1
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,]

====== Limited PosiCode

Limited PosiCode A:

....
Data:    ABC-12.3
Options: version=limiteda
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cg==]

Limited PosiCode B:

....
Data:    ABC-12.3
Options: version=limitedb
Encoder: posicode
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cg==]

==== Telepen

*Telepen* is an arbitrary length barcode symbology for encoding all 128
ASCII characters without the need for shift characters.

Also known as: Telepen Alpha, Telepen Full ASCII.

Uses:

* Library books and library cards, chiefly in UK libraries.

Variants:

* <<_telepen_numeric,Telepen Numeric>> is a variant for efficient
encoding of numeric data.

Standards: USS Telepen.

===== Data and Options

* The data can contain any standard ASCII data, values 0-127.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The mandatory check digit is automatically included.
* _Deprecated: Use <<_telepen_numeric,Telepen Numeric>> instead. When
the *numeric* option is given, the data is read as either pairs of
digits or `0X`, `1X`, etc. The singular values `^000` to `^015` and
`^127` can also be encoded using the _parse_ option._

===== Examples

A basic symbol:

....
Data:    Telepen
Options: includetext
Encoder: telepen
....

==== Telepen Numeric

*Telepen Numeric* is a variant of the Telepen symbology for efficient
encoding of numeric data.

Variants:

* <<_telepen,Telepen>> is the full ASCII form.

Standards: USS Telepen.

===== Data and Options

* The data is provided as pairs of digits, where the second digit of a
pair may be `X`, as in `0X`, `1X`, etc. The singular values `^000` to
`^015` and `^127` can also be encoded using the _parse_ option.
* With the _parse_ option, `^016` (DLE) switches the rest of the data to
full ASCII, for example for an odd final digit or a suffix. It cannot be
the first character.
* When the *parse* option is specified, any instances of `^NNN` in the
data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for
specifying unprintable characters.
* The mandatory check digit is automatically included.

===== Examples

A symbol encoding pairs of digits:

....
Data:    123456
Options:
Encoder: telepennumeric
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

A symbol encoding data that includes X digits:

....
Data:    1X345X
Options:
Encoder: telepennumeric
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Kodak Patch Codes

The *symbol* encoder generates the patch codes that Kodak document
scanners recognise to separate batches and to switch scanning modes.

Uses:

* Separator sheets that assign an image level to a document in a batch,
or that switch between bi-tonal and colour scanning.

Standards: Kodak A-61599, Patch Code Information for Kodak Scanners.

===== Data and Options

* The data field accepts one of the following values:
** `patch1` - Patch 1
** `patch2` - Patch 2, which assigns image level 2 to the current
document
** `patch3` - Patch 3, which assigns image level 3 to the current
document
** `patch4` - Patch 4, the toggle patch
** `patch6` - Patch 6
** `patcht` - Patch T, the transfer patch, which assigns the predefined
image level to the next document
* The symbol is drawn at its specified size: bars and spaces 0.08 or
0.20 inches wide, 0.80 inches in all, with bars 2.5 inches long.
Scanners require the bars to be parallel to the leading edge of the
document and at least 0.25 inches from other printing.

===== Examples

Patch 2:

....
Data:    patch2
Options:
Encoder: symbol
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

The transfer patch:

....
Data:    patcht
Options:
Encoder: symbol
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

The toggle patch:

....
Data:    patch4
Options:
Encoder: symbol
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

==== VIN

The *Vehicle Identification Number (VIN)* symbol is a
<<_code_39,Code 39>> barcode, without a symbol check character, carrying
the 17-character number that identifies a road vehicle.

Uses:

* Vehicle labels and documents.

Standards: ISO 3779 Road vehicles - Vehicle identification number (VIN)
- Content and structure; US 49 CFR Part 565 Vehicle Identification
Number (VIN) Requirements. These define the number; its Code 39 form is
industry practice.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the 17-character VIN, of digits and upper case
letters other than I, O and Q.
* The check digit in the ninth position is required of every vehicle for
the US market, and is verified when the World Manufacturer Identifier
begins with a digit from 1 to 5, for North America. Elsewhere the ninth
position may be any VIN character.
* The options of <<_code_39,Code 39>> are available, such as *hidestars*
to omit the asterisks from the human readable text, except for those of
the symbol check character.

===== Examples

....
Data:    1ZZAB12C8DE345678
Options: includetext
Encoder: vin
....

==== LOGMARS

*LOGMARS* (Logistics Applications of Automated Marking and Reading
Symbols) is the use of <<_code_39,Code 39>> by the US Department of
Defense for marking unit packs, outer containers and documents.

Uses:

* US Department of Defense marking of unit packs, outer containers and
documents.

Standards: MIL-STD-1189B Standard Department of Defense Bar Code
Symbology.

===== Data and Options

* The data field can contain the characters of <<_code_39,Code 39>>:
digits, upper case letters, space and `-`, `.`, `$`, `/`, `{plus}`, `%`,
up to 30 characters including any check character.
* The human readable text omits the start and stop characters, as the
standard requires.
* The *includecheck* option adds the optional modulo 43 check character.
The other options of <<_code_39,Code 39>> are available.
* The X-dimension of the standard for general applications is from
0.190mm to 0.508mm. Under the physical specification options the minimum
height is that of the density of the X-dimension: 6.35mm from 6.5
characters per inch, 9.53mm from 3.0, and 19.05mm below.

===== Examples

....
Data:    BOX 42 OF 100
Options: includetext
Encoder: logmars
....

==== DX Film Edge

The *DX Film Edge* barcode is exposed as a latent image along the edge
of 135 (35mm) photographic film to identify the film for automated
photofinishing, as a data track beside a clock track that synchronises
its reading.

Uses:

* Identification of the film and its frames in automated photofinishing
of 135 film.

Standards: ISO 1007 Photography - 135-size film and magazine -
Specifications; US Patent 4,965,628.

===== Data and Options

* The data field is the DX number, optionally followed by `/` and the
frame number:
** The DX number is either its two parts separated by a hyphen, Part 1,
the product code, from 1 to 127 and Part 2, the generation, from 0 to
15, e.g. `79-7`; or the DX extract of up to four digits, e.g. `1271`; or
the six digits of the full DX number, e.g. `012710`, whose first and
last digits are not encoded.
** The frame number is from 0 to 63, optionally followed by `A` for a
half frame. `S` and `X` stand for frame 62, `K` and `00` for frame 63,
and `F` for frame 0.
* The *rowheight* option specifies the height of each track in modules.
The default is 3.

===== Examples

....
Data:    79-7/22A
Options:
Encoder: dxfilmedge
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}Cg==]

Without a frame number:

....
Data:    1271
Options:
Encoder: dxfilmedge
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

=== GS1 Composite Symbols

*GS1 Composite* barcode symbologies consist of a primary component
beneath a 2D component (variations of <<_micropdf417,MicroPDF417>> and
<<_pdf417,PDF417>>) used to encode supplementary
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 formatted data>>.

Uses:

* Small healthcare items, such as vials and ampoules, carrying a batch
and expiry date with the GTIN; consider
<<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>>, which GS1 prefers.

Variants:

* <<_ean_13_composite,EAN-13 Composite>> is a variant of
<<_ean_13,EAN-13>>.
* <<_ean_8_composite,EAN-8 Composite>> is a variant of <<_ean_8,EAN-8>>.
* <<_upc_a_composite,UPC-A Composite>> is a variant of <<_upc_a,UPC-A>>.
* <<_upc_e_composite,UPC-E Composite>> is a variant of <<_upc_e,UPC-E>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_omnidirectional_composite,GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional Composite>>
is a variant of
<<_gs1_databar_omnidirectional,GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_stacked_omnidirectional_composite,GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional Composite>>
is a variant of
<<_gs1_databar_stacked_omnidirectional,GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_expanded_composite,GS1 DataBar Expanded Composite>> is
a variant of <<_gs1_databar_expanded,GS1 DataBar Expanded>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_expanded_stacked_composite,GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked Composite>>
is a variant of
<<_gs1_databar_expanded_stacked,GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_truncated_composite,GS1 DataBar Truncated Composite>>
is a variant of <<_gs1_databar_truncated,GS1 DataBar Truncated>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_stacked_composite,GS1 DataBar Stacked Composite>> is a
variant of <<_gs1_databar_stacked,GS1 DataBar Stacked>>.
* <<_gs1_databar_limited_composite,GS1 DataBar Limited Composite>> is a
variant of <<_gs1_databar_limited,GS1 DataBar Limited>>.
* <<_gs1_128_composite,GS1-128 Composite>> is a variant of
<<_gs1_128,GS1-128>>.

Data syntax:
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifiers>>.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24723, ITS EAN.UCC Composite Symbology, AIM ISS -
EAN.UCC Composite Symbology, GS1 General Specifications.

===== Data and Options

* The data field consists of a primary and secondary component separated
by a pipe `++|++` character.
* The data for the primary component (preceding the pipe) is entered in
a format identical to the corresponding non-composite barcode symbology.
* The data for the 2D component (following the pipe) is entered in
<<_gs1_application_identifier_standard_format,GS1 Application Identifier standard format>>.
* Note that it is not necessary to specify _FNC1_ characters since the
encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
* _Deprecated._ The *dontlint* option disables GS1 Application
Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input
that does not comply with GS1 standards.
* For maximum efficiency, if the data for the 2D component contains a
number of application identifiers matching any of the specifications
below then they should be provided in this given order:
** `(11)...(10)...`
** `(17)...(10)...`
** `(90)++{++0-3 digits not starting 0}++{++upper alpha}...`
* The *ccversion* option is used to select a specific 2D component, and
is normally left to the default:
** `ccversion=a` - <<_cc_a,CC-A>>
** `ccversion=b` - <<_cc_b,CC-B>>
** `ccversion=c` - <<_cc_c,CC-C>>
(<<_gs1_128_composite,GS1-128 Composite>> only)
** If *ccversion* is not specified a CC-A component will be selected if
the data will fit, otherwise a CC-B component will be used. In the case
of <<_gs1_128_composite,GS1-128 Composite>> a CC-C component will be
used if the data does not fit within either a CC-A or CC-B component.
* The *gs1-cc* encoder draws the 2D component alone, and its *cccolumns*
option sets the component's width in columns: 2 to 4 for CC-A and CC-B,
and up to 30 for CC-C.

==== EAN-13 Composite

....
Data:    9520123456788|(99)1234-abcd
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13composite
....

==== EAN-8 Composite

....
Data:    95200002|(21)A12345678
Options: includetext guardwhitespace

=== Raw Symbols

==== DAFT

*DAFT* is an encoder for directly specifying the sequence of descender,
ascender, full-height and tracker bars of a custom 4 state barcode
symbol.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains a sequence of the characters `D`, `A`, `F` or
`T` to denote the descender, ascender, full-height and tracker bars of a
custom 4 state symbol.

===== Examples

A custom 4-state symbol:

....
Data:    FATDAFTDAD
Options:
Encoder: daft
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNTIiIGhlaWdodD0iMTMiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA1MiAxMyI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjIiIHk9Ii0xLjMiIHdpZHRoPSI2Mi40IiBoZWlnaHQ9IjE1LjYiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}CjxwYXRoIGZpbGwtcnVsZT0ibm9uemVybyIgZmlsbD0icmdiKDEwMCUsIDEwMCUsIDEwMCUpIiBmaWxsLW9wYWNpdHk9IjEiIGQ9Ik0gMCAxMyBMIDUxLjI0NjA5NCAxMyBMIDUxLjI0NjA5NCAwLjM5ODQzOCBMIDAgMC4zOTg0MzggWiBNIDAgMTMgIi8{plus}{plus}Cjwvc3ZnPgo=]

==== Flattermarken

*Flattermarken* are identification marks used in book production that
facilitate the proper arrangement of bound sections by a book binder.

===== Data and Options

* The data field holds a sequence of digits, each a group of nine
modules:
** `1-9`: a single mark at that module of the group
** `0`: the group is left blank
* The *inkspread* option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.
* If greater fidelity is required then the <<_raw,raw>> encoder should
be used instead.

===== Examples

Marks in the first, second and fourth groups, at modules 1, 3 and 4:

....
Data:    1304
Options: inkspread=-1
Encoder: flattermarken
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz4KPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHhtbG5zOnhsaW5rPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8xOTk5L3hsaW5rIiB3aWR0aD0iNTEiIGhlaWdodD0iMjIiIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCA1MSAyMiI{plus}CjxyZWN0IHg9Ii01LjEiIHk9Ii0yLjIiIHdpZHRoPSI2MS4yIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjI2LjQiIGZpbGw9InJnYigxMDAlLCAxMDAlLCAxMDAlKSIgZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5PSIxIi8{plus}]

==== Raw

The *raw* encoder is used for directly specifying the space/bar
succession of a custom barcode symbol.

===== Data and Options

* The data field contains an alternating sequence of widths (1 to 9) for
the bars and spaces of a custom symbol, starting with a bar, in modules.

===== Examples

A custom barcode specifying bar/space widths directly:

....
Data:    331132131313411122131311333213114131131221323
Options: height=0.5
Encoder: raw
....

image:data:image/svg+xml;base64,[data:image/svg{plus}xml;base64,{plus}]

=== Partial Symbols

==== EAN-2

*EAN-2* is the two-digit add-on code that accompanies an EAN or UPC type
barcode symbol such as an <<_issn,ISSN>>.

Also known as: Two-Digit Add-On, Two-Digit Supplement, UPC-2.

Uses:

* The issue number of a magazine or other periodical, beside its ISSN or
UPC barcode.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, GS1 General Specifications.

Note: The use of a two-digit add-on with EAN-8 is not defined by any
symbology standard.

_Deprecated._ Standalone use of the EAN-2 encoder is discouraged. It is
better to include an add-on by specifying the supplement's value as an
extension to the data for the primary symbol. For example,
`0317-8471 03 17` for a symbol representing the ISSN 0317-8471 (having
sequence number 03) and with issue number 17 denoted using a two-digit
add-on.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must contain two digits.
* For a periodical, the add-on usually carries the issue number, such as
`01` to `12` for a monthly or `01` to `53` for a weekly, according to
the
https://ppa.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/PPA_Best_Practice_for_Bar_Code_Guidelines.pdf[PPA's
barcoding guidelines].
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.

===== Examples

A standalone two-digit add-on:

....
Data:    05
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean2
....

==== EAN-5

*EAN-5* is the five-digit add-on code that accompanies an EAN or UPC
type barcode symbol such as an <<_isbn,ISBN>> or <<_issn,ISSN>>.

Also known as: Five-Digit Add-On, Five-Digit Supplement, UPC-5.

Uses:

* The suggested retail price of a book, beside its ISBN barcode.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, GS1 General Specifications.

Note: The use of a five-digit add-on with EAN-8 is not defined by any
symbology standard.

_Deprecated._ Standalone use of the EAN-5 encoder is discouraged. It is
better to include an add-on by specifying the supplement's value as an
extension to the data for the primary symbol. For example,
`978-1-873671-00-9 54499` for a symbol representing the ISBN
978-1-873671-00-9 with suggested retail price $44.99 denoted using a
five-digit add-on.

===== Data and Options

* The data field must contain five digits.
* For a book, the add-on carries the suggested retail price, according
to the
https://www.bisg.org/barcoding-guidelines-for-the-us-book-industry[BISG
barcoding guidelines]: `5` followed by the price in US cents, such as
`51995` for $19.95; `90000` when there is no suggested price; and
`59999` for a price above $99.98, which is then not encoded. `00000` and
`50000` are not used.
* The *includetext* option should normally be supplied.

===== Examples

A standalone five-digit add-on:

....
Data:    90200
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean5
....

==== GS1 Application Identifier Standard Format

Certain barcode symbologies (including <<_gs1_128,GS1-128>>,
<<_gs1_databar_expanded,GS1 DataBar Expanded>>,
<<_gs1_datamatrix,GS1 DataMatrix>>, <<_gs1_qr_code,GS1 QR Code>> and
<<_gs1_composite_symbols,GS1 Composite Symbols>>) represent standardized
GS1 data and require that their data field is provided in GS1
Application Identifier standard format, consisting of a concatenated
string of _AIs_ along with their corresponding values.

The AIs are a set of several hundred two-, three- or four-digit prefixes
written within parentheses that represent physical attributes and
business information, e.g.

* _(00)_ is an eighteen-digit SSCC.
* _(01)_ is a fourteen-digit GTIN. A GTIN-13, GTIN-12 or GTIN-8 is
written zero-filled on the left to fourteen digits.
* _(403)_ is a variable-length routing code.

The following input represents GTIN-14 _09521234543213_; Expiration Date
_1 January 2010_; Batch _123ABC_; Serial _1234567890_:

....
(01)09521234543213(17)100101(10)123ABC(21)1234567890
....

Encoders for barcode symbologies that expect data in GS1 Application
Identifier standard format will take care of parsing the input and
inserting any necessary _FNC1_ characters to delimit variable length
fields.

===== Encoding parentheses within Application Identifier data values

Instances of parentheses, `(` and `)`, within Application Identifier
data values must be escaped using the <<_parse,parse option>> as `^040`
and `^041`, respectively.

===== GS1 Application Identifier Linting

The input is checked against the structural rules for the GS1
Application Identifiers, as given in the
https://github.com/gs1/gs1-syntax-dictionary[GS1 Barcode Syntax
Dictionary], unless the *dontlint* option is given. AIs that are
mutually exclusive are refused. The Application Identifier definitions
are provided in the https://ref.gs1.org/standards/genspecs/[GS1 General
Specifications].

===== Use of Group Separator character (GS; ASCII 29) as an AI separator

FNC1 is the canonical AI separator in GS1 symbols, and BWIPP always
encodes it. GS characters are tolerated as separators by the GS1
standards but not encouraged, and can produce larger symbols.

Where an application nevertheless requires GS separators, the message
can be encoded manually with a general (non-GS1) encoder, without the
benefit of BWIPP's validation of the AI data:

....
Data:    ^FNC1095212345432131710010110123ABC^GS211234567890
Options: parse parsefnc
Encoder: datamatrix
....
